The Hindu Musical Scale and the twenty-two Shrutees. Page 40.
“Shrutes may be more than twenty-two also, this number being the one generally accepted, some Sanskrit authors recognising 42, some 66 and some saying that they are innumerable.”
“curutikaḷ 22-kkum atikamāyirukkalām. āṉāl 22 eṉṟu cātāraṇa māy oppuk koḷḷappaṭṭirukkiṟatu, cila camaskiru kirantakarttākkaḷ 42 curutikaḷ eṉṟum, cilar 66 eṉṟum iṉṉum cilar eṇṇiṟanta curutikaḷ uṇṭu eṉṟum collukiṟārkaḷ.”
mēṟkāṭṭiya varikaḷil 22 curutikaḷukku mēlāka irukkalām eṉṟum cātāraṇamāy 22 eṉṟu oppukkoḷḷappaṭukiṟa teṉṟum, ataṟkumēl 42 eṉṟum, 66 eṉṟum, curutikaḷ eṇṇiṟantavai eṉṟum collukiṟār. itaṉāl oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷuṇṭeṉṟu coṉṉa cāraṅkatēvarai avar vīṟṟirukkum uṉṉata pīṭattiliruntu talaikīḻākat taḷḷi nīṅkaḷ alaikkaḻikkiṟīrkaḷeṉṟu teḷivākat terikiṟatu. mēlum 22 curutikaḷukkum mēlāka atikamāṉa curutikaḷait tāṅkaḷ kaṇṭupiṭittatāka aṭiyil varum vacaṉattāl teḷivākac collukiṟīrkaḷ.
The Hindu Musical scale and the twenty two Srutis, Introduction by E.Clements, Page 2.
“Mr.Krishnaji Mahadev Gokhale of Miraj who makes use of considerably more than 22 Srutis has kindly sung over to me 83 Ragas and Raginis and given me the names of the notes used in them.”
“22 curutikaḷukku atikamāṉa curutikaḷai upayōkikkum mirāj paṭṭaṇattu Krishnaji Mahadev Gokhaleeṉpavar 83 rākaṅkaḷ rākiṉikaḷai eṉakkup pāṭik kāṇpittatumallāmal avaikaḷil upayōkappaṭum curaṅkaḷiṉ pērkaḷaiyum eṉakkuk koṭuttār.”
‘mirāj paṭṭaṇattu kiruṣṇāji makātēva kōkkalē eṉpavar 93 irākaṅkaḷaip pāṭikkāṭṭi avaikaḷil vaḻaṅkum curaṅkaḷukkup peyar kaḷaiyum eṉakkuk koṭuttār’ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. itil 22 curuti kaḷuṇṭeṉṟa caṅkīta ratṉākarar apippirāyamum kirakam māṟṟukaiyil 25 curutikaḷ kaṇṭu piṭittēṉ eṉṟa taṅkaḷ apippirāyamum aṭipaṭṭup pōkāmal nilaittirukkiṉṟaṉavā? ivaikaḷ yāvaṟṟaiyum muṉpiṉ ārāyntu pārkkāmal caṅkīta ratṉākararaiyum parataraiyum uyarnta pīṭattil vaikkiṟīrkaḷ. uḷ nuḻaintu pārttāl tāṅkaḷum Mr.tēvālum avarkaḷ iruvaruṭaiya kaḻuttilum curukkiṭṭut terut teruvāy iḻuttu avamāṉam ceykiṟīrkaḷ. aṭiyil varum cila varikaḷaik kavaṉittāl ataṟku mēlum ceykiṟīrkaḷeṉṟu teḷivāyt terikiṟatu.
Introduction to the study of Indian Music Page. 2.
The present work deals with Hindustani Music only; the author hopes to be able to show that a great part of it is directly traceable to the systems set forth in Bharata’s Natya Shastra of about the fifth century A.D. and the Sangit Ratnakar of the thirteenth century. These are the most closely reasoned and critically worded of the early text books.
inta nūl intustāṉ caṅkītattaippaṟṟi māttiram pēcukiṟatu. atil colliyirukkum anēka kāriyaṅkaḷ 5-m nūṟṟāṇṭiluḷḷa parata nāṭṭiya cāstirattilum, 13-m nūṟṟāṇṭiluḷḷa caṅkīta ratṉākarattilum colliyirukkum muṟaikaḷiṉiṉṟu eṭukkappaṭṭavaikaḷtāṉ. āti kirantaṅkaḷil inta iraṇṭu nūlkaḷtāṉ takunta niyāyatāraṅkaḷuḷḷavai yum ārāycciyuḷḷavaikaḷumāy irukkiṉṟaṉa.
caṅkīta rattiṉākaramum, parata cāstiramum takunta niyāya ātāraṅkaḷum ārāycciyumuḷḷavaiyeṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. inta nūlkaḷai ātāramākak koṇṭē tāṅkaḷ intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟku nūl eḻutukiṟa tākac collukiṟīrkaḷ. aṭutta vākkiyattil caṅkīta ratṉākarattai ārāyntu pārttāl atu intustāṉ caṅkītattaippaṟṟic collukiṟa teṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. itu evvaḷavu tūram uṇmaiyā yirukkumeṉṟu nām pārkka vēṇṭum.
Introduction to the study of Indian Music Page 2.
“It is reputed that Sarangdev, the author of the Sangit Ratnakar, was an inhabitant of Kashmir. From internal evidence one would conclude that the Music he describes is that of Hindustan. However, the pandits of southern India endeavour to appropriate him to themselves. The present writer hopes to show that it is only by doing violence to his theory that it can be applied to Karnatic Music.”
“caṅkīta ratṉākaram eḻutiṉa cāraṅkatēvar kāṣmīr nakaravāci eṉpatu yāvarukkum terinta viṣayam. nūliṉuḷ ārāyntu pārttāl avar collu kiṟatu intustāṉ caṅkītattaip paṟṟi, āṉāl teṉṉintiya caṅkīta paṇṭitarkaḷ avar taṅkaḷaic cērntavar eṉṟu collik koḷḷa muyaṟcik kiṟārkaḷ. innūlai eḻutukiṟavar eṉṉa rūpikkap pōkiṟā reṉṟāl, avaruṭaiya koḷkaikku muṟṟum virōtamāṉa oṉṟaic coṉṉāltāṉ atu karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṟku ēṟṟatāka muṭiyum.”
cāraṅkatēvar tēvakiri eṉṟa ūril cimmaṇarājaṉ kālattil 1207-1249 varaiyum camastāṉa vitvāṉāyiruntatākavum akkālattil innūl eḻutappaṭṭatākavum terikiṟatu. 1294kku mēl vintiyamalaikkut teṉpākam makamatiyarkaḷ paṭaiyeṭuttu vantārkaḷēyoḻiya ataṟkumuṉ aṅku varavillai. avarkaḷ vantapiṉ tēvakirikku araṅkapāttaic cērnta taulatapāt eṉṟu peyar vaḻaṅkiṟṟu. itaṉāl intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟku eṉṟu annūl eḻutappaṭṭatallaveṉṟu terikiṟatu. avar intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟku eḻutiyiruppārāṉāl intustāṉ pāṣai pēcuvōr vaḻaṅkum teyvaṅkaḷiṉ peyar, mukkiyamāṉa rājākkaḷiṉ peyar, avar kālattilirunta navāpiṉ peyar mutaliyavaikaḷaṉaittum nūliṉ colli yiruppārē. avar appaṭic collāmal intukkaḷuṭaiya teyvaṅkaḷaiyum muṉivarkaḷaiyum maṟṟum intukkaḷuṭaiya paḻakka vaḻakkaṅ kaḷaiyumē muṟṟum colliyirukkiṟār. atōṭu pūrva tamiḻnāṭṭil vaḻaṅki vanta pala irākaṅkaḷil takka eṉpatai ṭakka eṉṟum, nāṭṭarākam eṉpatai nāṭṭai eṉṟum, cātāri eṉpatai rūpacātāri, cutta cātāri eṉṟum, vairavam eṉpatai pairavam eṉṟum, kuṟiñci eṉpatai kurāñci eṉṟum, intaḷam eṉpatai ittōḷam eṉṟum, taṉāci eṉpatai taṉṉiyāci eṉṟum, iṉṉum ivaipōl pala paṇkaḷiṉ peyarkaḷaiyum māṟṟi avar vaḻaṅki yirukkiṟār.
itōṭu irākacañcāram colvatai nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl tamiḻ nāṭṭil vaḻaṅki vanta vairavam, varāṭi, takkarākam, intaḷam pōṉṟa irākaṅ kaḷukku ilakṣaṇam collukiṟār. avvirākaṅkaḷiṉ curaṅkaḷum curutikaḷum tamiḻ muṟaippaṭi colliyiruppārāṉāl ellōrukkum upayōkappaṭak kūṭiyatāyirukkum. irākaṅkaḷiṉ alaku muṟaiyum 22 curutiyil colvatiṉāl avaikaḷai muṟṟilum aṉupōkattiṟku varāmal taḷḷumpaṭi nēriṭṭatu.
vēkarañci eṉṟa irākattiṟkuc collum ilakṣaṇattaiyum cura cañcārattaiyum nām kavaṉippōmāṉāl avaikaḷ mēkarañcaṉi eṉṟu taṟkālattil vaḻaṅkum irākattiṟkuriyavaiyāyirukkiṉṟaṉa. itait tamiḻ makkaḷ mēka irākam eṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷ. mēka irākam eṉṟa pūrva peyarai mēkarañci eṉṟum, vēkarañci eṉṟum māṟṟiṉatēyoḻiya maṟṟappaṭi irākacañcāram mūṉṟukkum oṉṟākavē irukkiṟateṉṟu kāṇpōm. āṉāl 22 curuti muṟaiyil ivaikaḷ pāṭa muṟṟilum kūṭāta kāriyameṉṟu terikiṟatu.
tamiḻnāṭṭil vaḻaṅkivanta paṇkaḷaiyum, irākaṅkaḷaiyum, colla vantavar tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta 24 curutikaḷ iṉṉavaiyeṉṟu aṟintu koḷḷāmal oru stāyiyil 22 eṉṟu mēḷam kaṭṭic coṉṉatiṉālē muṟṟilum avar nūl upayōkappaṭāmal pōyviṭṭatu. teṉṉintiya caṅkīta muṟaippaṭi annūl upayōkappaṭavēṇṭumāṉāl kāntārak kirāmattait tēṭip pōyirukkum caṅkīta ratṉākararai varavaḻaittu, 24 curuti muṟaippaṭi, tāṅkaḷ collum ilakṣaṇaṅkaḷait tiruttik koṭukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu kēṭṭāl tiruntumēyoḻiya vēṟu evvitattilum avar nūl aṉupōkattiṟku varātu. intastāṉ caṅkītam paṭippōrkaḷukku avar eḻutavumillai. avar muṟaippaṭi intustāṉ caṅkītamirukkavumillai. intustāṉ caṅkītam paṭippōr itil mayaṅka villai eṉṟu intiya ārmōṉiyattait taḷḷiṉatiṉāl aṟintu cantōṣappaṭukiṟēṉ. caṅkīta ratṉākararaiyum parataraiyum cariyāṉa niyāya ātārattōṭu uyarnta pīṭattil vaitta tāṅkaḷ avarḷai avamāṉap paṭuttukiṟīrkaḷeṉṟu itaṉpiṉ varum taṅkaḷ vacaṉattāl teḷivāyk kāṇkiṟōm.
Introduction to the study of Indian Music, Introduction, Page XIII.
“Modern text books may appear learned to the uninitiated; the historian will, however, frankly admit that, since the days of the Sangit Ratnakar, Indian Musical systems have fallen into such confusion that no one has been able to reconcile the teaching of that authoritative treatise with latter works on the subject or with the practice or theory of modern musicians.”
“cūṭcumam teriyātavarkaḷukkut taṟkāla caṅkīta nūlkaḷ veku kalvittiṟamai yuḷḷavaikaḷāyk kāṇappaṭalām. āṉāl carittirakkāraṉ etai veḷippaṭaiyāy oppuk koḷḷuvāṉeṉṟāl, caṅkīta ratṉākaram tōṉṟiya nāḷ mutal intiya caṅkīta muṟaikaḷ catā cantēkattukku iṭamāyviṭṭatu. mūla nūleṉṟum atikāra nūl eṉṟum oppuk koḷḷappaṭṭa caṅkīta ratṉākarattukkum pintiṉa nūlkaḷukkum yātoru campantamumillai yeṉpatu māttiramalla, anta nūlukkum taṟkāla cāstira aṉupōkaṅkaḷukkuṅkūṭa koñcamākilum campantamē yillai.”
‘caṅkīta ratṉākaram tōṉṟiya nāḷ mutal intiya caṅkīta muṟaikaḷ catā cantēkattiṟ kiṭamāyiṟṟu’ eṉṟu eḻutukiṟīrkaḷ. itu uṇmaiyē. oru stāyiyil 12 curaṅkaḷ amaittu irupattu nāṉkum nāṟpat teṭṭum toṇṇūṟṟāṟumāṉa curutikaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta tamiḻ muṟaikkum oru stāyiyil 22 eṉṟu coṉṉa caṅkīta ratṉākarar muṟaikkum eppaṭip poruntum? pūrva tamiḻ muṟaippaṭiyē taṟkāla aṉupōka muṟaiyirukkiṟa teṉṟu kaṇṭa pārijātakkārar, vēṅkaṭamaki pōṉṟavarkaḷ caṅkīta ratṉā karattāl aṉupōkattilirukkum caṅkītattiṟku āpattu varum eṉṟu kaṇṭu pūrvam tamiḻmakkaḷ pāṭikkoṇṭirunta muṟaiyilum yāḻilum kaṇṭapaṭi 12 curaṅkaḷaiyē stāpittārkaḷ. eṉṟālum nuṭpa curaṅkaḷ iṉṉavaiyeṉṟu kaṇṭukoḷḷa muṭiyāmal pōṉārkaḷ.
12 curaṅkaḷōṭu varum nuṭpa curaṅkaḷai tuvāvimcati curutiyil cērttu viṭalāmeṉṟu teṉṉintiyāviluḷḷa cilar mikavum pirayācap paṭṭārkaḷ. eṉṟālum aṉupōkattiṟkuk kāṭṭamuṭiyāmal veṟum vāyp pēccōṭu niṉṟuviṭṭārkaḷ. tuvāvimcati curutiyeṉṟu coṉṉa pūrva nūlkaḷai stāpippataṟkut taṅkaḷ pūṇūhlaip piṭittuc cattiyam ceytu koṇṭārkaḷ. cattiyam paṇṇic cātippavai muṟṟilum poyyā yirukku mōveṉṟu cantēkikka iṭaṅkoṭukkiṟatē. āṉāl tāṅkaḷ uḷḷatu uḷḷapaṭiyē paratam caṅkīta ratṉākaram eṉṟa nūlkaḷukkum ataṟkup pintiṉa nūlkaḷukkum yātoru campantamumillai eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. atōṭu aṉupōkattiṟkum koñcamāvatu campantamillai eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷē colliviṭṭu avar nūlai ātāramākak koṇṭu uṇṭākkiya ārmōṉiyamum aṉupōkattiṟku ottuvarāmal taḷḷappaṭṭatē. itu uṇmaiyē. ivvuṇmaiyaip piratyaṭcamāyk kaṇṭa tāṅkaḷ avarai uyarnta pīṭattil vaittu tāḻat taḷḷukiṟīrkaḷ.
aṉupōkattiṟku varāta oru cāstirattai ulakattil etaṟku nām oppiṭuvatu? viṣamum kūṭa oru maruntiṟku utavukiṟatē. appaṭikkūṭa illaiyē. pōrāṭṭattiṟkeṉṟu oru cāstiram eḻuti vaippārkaḷā? oru stāyiyil curutikaḷ irupattu nāṉkāy vaittuc cāraṅkar eḻuti yiruppārāṉāl pūrva tamiḻ nūl eḻutiya makāṉkaḷukkup piṉ ivarum oruvarāka eṇṇappaṭuvār eṉpataṟkuc cantēkamillai. 22 eppaṭi aṉu pōkattilillātirukkiṟatō appaṭiyē tāṅkaḷ kaṇṭupiṭitta irupat taintu mirukkiṟatu. itōṭu intiyāvil vīṇai vācippavarkaḷālum vāyppāṭṭup pāṭukiṟa vitvāṉkaḷālum caṅkīta ratṉākaram taḷḷappaṭukiṟa teṉṟu aṭiyil kaṇṭa vacaṉattil collukiṟīrkaḷ.
Introduction to the study of Indian music Page 82.
“Nowadays among the practical musicians of western India, the Sangit Ratnakar is looked upon as belonging to a bygene age although no one is able to say what it is which makes its theories inapplicable to modern practice. Professional musicians have constructed their own systems; needless to say, they differ widely one from another.”
“taṟkālam mēl intiyāviṉ vīṇai vāyppāṭṭu vitvāṉkaḷ caṅkīta ratṉākaram eṉṟa nūlai upayōkattilillāta aḻintu pōṉa paḻaiya nūl eṉṟu niṉaikkiṟārkaḷ. āṉāl ēṉ atil collap paṭṭirukkiṟa muṟaikkum taṟkāla aṉupōkattiṟkum kiñcittēṉum campanta millai yeṉpataṟkuk kāraṇam collakkūṭātavarkaḷāyirukkiṟārkaḷ. caṅkītattaiyē toḻilākak koṇṭa anēka vitvāṉkaḷ taṅkaḷukkut tōṉṟiya muṟaikaḷai uṇṭākki yirukkiṟārkaḷ. ākaiyāl avai oṉṟaṟkoṉṟu aṉanta vittiyācamuḷḷavaikaḷāyirukkiṉṟaṉa.”
mēṟkaṇṭa vacaṉattil ‘caṅkīta ratṉākaram eṉṟa nūlai upayōkatti lillāta aḻintu pōṉa paḻaiya nūl eṉṟu niṉaikkiṟārkaḷ’ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. caṅkīta cāstiraṅkaḷ yāvaṟṟilum vīṇaiyai uyarvākac collappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. maṉuṭa cārīrattāl collakkūṭiya iṉiya nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷaiyum vīṇaiyil collalām. maṟṟa vāttiyaṅkaḷil colla muṭiyāta neṭil kuṟil oṟṟukkaḷum iṉṉum niṉaikkakkūṭiya iṉiya ōcaikaḷum vīṇaiyil collappaṭak kūṭiyatāyiruppataṉāl atai uyiruḷḷa vāttiyameṉṟum tēvavāttiyam eṉṟum coṉṉārkaḷ. maṉitaṉai tēvavāttiyameṉṟum allatu kāttira vīṇaiyeṉṟum maṉuṭa carīrattai ottirukkum ceṅkōṭṭiyāḻai tāru vīṇaiyeṉṟum cāma vētattiṉ tuvakkattil collappaṭṭirukkiṟatē. ippaṭi mēṉmai poruntiya vīṇai vācikkum vaiṇīkarkaḷum pāṭakarkaḷum caṅkīta ratṉākaram aṉupōkattiṟku varāmal aḻintu pōṉa paḻaiya nūl eṉṟu colvatai muṟṟilum kavaṉiyāmal tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta ratṉākarar muṟaiyai eṭuttu niṟuttuvatākac collukiṟīrkaḷ. pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ yāḻ eṉṟu vaḻaṅki vanta vāttiyattai vīṇai yeṉṟu taṟkālattavar vaḻaṅki varukiṟārkaḷ.
caṅkīta ratṉākarar muṟaikkum taṟkāla aṉupōkattiṟkum kiñcit tēṉum campantamillai eṉṟu colvatē pōtātā? ataṟku mēl kāraṇamum vēṇṭumā? oru stāyiyai 24 camapākaṅkaḷāyp pirippataṟkum 22 āyp pirippataṟkum vittiyācamillaiyā? irupattu nāṉkāyp pirikkum poḻutu pañcamam 700 ceṉṭskaḷuṭaiyatākiṟatu. 22 curutikaḷāyp pirikkum poḻutu 709 ceṉṭskaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa. 2/3 muṟaiyāy 702 ceṉṭskaḷā kiṉṟaṉa. camamāyp pirittuk kirakam māṟṟip pāṭuvataṟkum, nuṭpa curaṅkaḷ kaṇittup pāṭuvataṟkum, aṉukūlamāka aṉupōkattilirukkum muṟaiyai maṉappāṭam ceytu pāṭikkoṇṭirukkum vitvāṉkaḷ aṟiyāmal pōṉatiṉāl kāraṇañ collakkūṭavillai. kāraṇam collātatiṉāl kaṟkaṇṭu kallākiviṭumā?
oru poruḷ naṉmaiyai viḷaikkumāṉāl nallateṉṟum keṭutiyai viḷaikkumāṉāl keṭṭa poruḷ eṉṟum aṉupōkattiṉā lēyē ulakattiṟku veḷippaṭaiyāyt terintirukkiṟatu. āṉāl avaikaḷiṉ talaiyil nallatu keṭṭatu eṉṟu eḻutiyirukkiṟatā? kaṟkaṇṭu eṉṟu peyar collāmal pōṉāl atu tappitamā? tāṅkaḷ kaṟkaṇṭu eṉṟu colli pāṣāṇattai vāyil pōṭukiṟatu pōlirukkiṟatu. intiya miyūcik kāṉpareṉsil tāṅkaḷ oru pāṣāṇattaip pakirntu koṭukka vantatākak kaṇṭōm. atu muṟṟilum kūṭāteṉṟu taṅkaḷ kaiyiliruntu ataip piṭuṅki eṟintōm. oruvarum cāppiṭak kūṭāteṉṟu vilakkiṉa nañcai paḻaiyapaṭi kaiyil eṭukkiṟatāka aṟintu varuttappaṭukiṟēṉ. iṉṉum intiyaṉ ārmōṉiyam eṉṟa nañcaik kaiyāṭuvīrkaḷāṉāl uṅkaḷ peyarai muṟṟilum keṭuttu viṭumēyeṉṟu aṉutāpappaṭukiṟēṉ.
aṉpuḷḷa turaiyē! ovvoṉṟāyk kavaṉittup pāruṅkaḷ. 22 curuti yeṉṟum 25 curuti yeṉṟum cātikkum taṅkaḷukkākavum eṉ conta jaṉaṅkaḷukkākavum ivaikaḷai eḻutukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ koñcam kavaṉittīr kaḷāṉāl nāṉ uṅkaḷukkuk koṭutta parōṭā kāṉpareṉs viyācaṅ kaḷil kaṇṭapaṭi Geometrical Progression il curam curutikaḷ varavēṇṭumeṉpatu viḷaṅkum. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta ratṉākararaiyum parataraiyum ēṟṟi iṟakkukiṟa tākak kāṇkiṟēṉ. avarkaḷai uṉṉatamāṉa stāṉattil tāṅkaḷ vaikkavillai. avarkaḷ tamiḻ nūlil colliya mēlāṉa karuttai aṟintukoḷḷāmal tavaṟippōṉavarkaḷ. taṅkaḷāl koṇṭāṭappaṭu kiṟārkaḷ. vaṭanāṭṭil vaḻaṅkum intustāṉ caṅkītattiṟkāka avar nūl eḻutavillai. ivaikaḷ yāvaṟṟiṟkum takunta kāraṇam kāṭṭit teṉṉintiya caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum curutikaḷaippaṟṟik karuṇāmirta cākaram mutal puttakattil iraṇṭām pākattil colliyirukkiṟēṉ.
tamiḻ makkaḷiṉ pūrvīkattilum avarkaḷiṉ nākarīkat tērcciyilum caṅkītattil avarkaḷ aṭainta payiṟciyilum maṟṟa ellāt tēcat tavarukkum muntiṉavareṉṟu aṅkē colliyirukkiṟēṉ. naṉṟāyk kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl tamiḻ makkaḷiṉ caṅkīta muṟai muṟṟilum Equal Temperament eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ ēḷaṉam ceyyum muṟai aṉṟu. aṅkē pōyc cāṭi maṟṟoru iṭattil viḻuntu eḻuntu vaḻivakai tōṉṟāmal ‘āṟṟil pōkum karaṭiyaik kampaḷi mūṭṭaiyeṉṟu kaṭṭippiṭittuk koṇṭāṉ’ eṉpatu pōlat tamiḻ makkaḷ taṅkaḷāl tūṣikkappaṭakkūṭiya pētaikaḷu malla. av vuttamamāṉa muṟaiyai eḻuti vaittavarkaḷait tāṅkaḷ parikācam ceyvataip pārkkilum tamiḻ makkaḷ yāvaraiyum parikācam ceyvatu ilēcāyirukkum.

paratarum cāraṅkatēvarum eḻutiya curuti muṟaiyil 13, 9, 4, 3, 2, 1 eṉpatākac collum kaṇakkē avarkaḷai uyarnta pīṭattil vaikkiṟa taṟkuk kāraṇam eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ. inta aḷavukaḷ avarkaḷ collātiruppārkaḷāṉāl mika naṉṟāyirukkum. ivvaḷavaikkoṇṭu oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ collumpoḻutu avar kuḻampukiṟa kuḻappat taiyum curutikaḷiṉ peyarkaḷaiyum ataṉ piṉ collappaṭum 19 curutikaḷukku viparamum irākaṅkaḷiṉ cañcārattiṟkuc collum lakṣaṇaṅ kaḷum iṉṉum oruvarālum aviḻkkappaṭāta muṭiccuppōl māttiramalla kiṭṭi neruṅkiyavarkaḷai iḻuttup pātāḷattil taḷḷum oru nīrc cuḻalaippōlavumirukkiṟatu. itil akappaṭṭa evarāvatu karaikaṇṭu kaṇṭavaikaḷaic colla ituvaraiyum muṉvaravillai. tāṅkaḷō avar nūlai uḷ nuḻaintupārttu veḷivantirukkiṟīrkaḷ. āṉāl kaṇṭavai kaḷaic collāmal tāṅkaḷ kalaṅkiṉa kalakkattiṉ payaṉāka 25 curuti eṉṟu maṟṟavarkaḷukkuc collukiṟīrkaḷ. avar arttañ ceytapaṭi tāṅkaḷ arttam ceytum ataṉ karuttu iṉṉateṉṟu kaṇṭu koḷḷāmal pōṉīrkaḷ.
1. ippōtu curutikaḷai aṟiyum viṣayattil cāraṅkar eṉṉa collu kiṟār? ataṟkup patil tāṅkaḷ eṉṉa collukiṟīrkaḷ? ataṉpiṉ ataṟku virōtamāy eṉṉa ceykiṟīrkaḷeṉṟu nām kavaṉikka vēṇṭum. cāraṅkar “22 tantikaḷ pōṭṭa vīṇaiyil mutal tantiyil uṉṉāl collakkūṭiya ārampa nātattai vai. ataṉpiṉ iṉṉum koñcam kūṭutalāka vai. ippaṭiyē nātattaik kūṭṭikkoṇṭupōka paṭippaṭiyāy oṉṟaṟkoṉṟu tīviramāy naṭuvil vēṟu nātamuṇṭākāmal 22 curutiyuṭaṉ oru stāyi amaikiṟatu” eṉṟu coṉṉār. ivar muṟai cama aḷavāṉa ōcaiyuṭaiyatā yirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu teḷivāyt terikiṟatu. avar appaṭic colliyiruppatiṉāl Geometrical Progression paṭiyē 22 curutikaḷ varavēṇṭum.
2. tāṅkaḷ oru stāyiyil varum curaṅkaḷ ca-pa oṟṟumaiyuṭaiya vaikaḷāyirukka vēṇṭum. appaṭiyāṉāl muṟṟilum cariyāṉa oṟṟumai yuḷḷa curaṅkaḷāl āṉavaikaḷāyirukkum. oru stāyiyil curaṅkaḷ cama aḷavuṭaiyatā yirukkavēṇṭumeṉṟu ēṇiyait tiṣṭāntap paṭuttik kāṭṭi yirukkiṟīrkaḷ. immuṟaiyil oru stāyiyiluḷḷa curaṅkaḷ camamāṉa ōcai aḷavuṭaiyatāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. appaṭic ceyvataṟku Geometrical Progression muṟaippaṭiyē avaikaḷirukka vēṇṭum. taṅkaḷ apippirāyattiṉpaṭiyē taṅkaḷukkuc ceyyat teriyāmal pōyviṭṭatu. nāṉō ceytu kāṭṭiyirukkiṟēṉ. pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ iṟṟaikku 2,000 varuṭaṅkaḷukku muṉ pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷāka immuṟai yaiyē paḻaki vantirukkiṟārkaḷ.
3. tāṅkaḷ curutikaḷ cama aḷavuṭaiyavaikaḷā yirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu taṅkaḷ puttakattil pala taṭavai colliyum maṟṟavarkaḷ tavaṟippōkāmal eccarittum oṟṟumaiyillāta curaṅkaḷaik kaṇṭu piṭikkum kuḻiyil viḻukiṟīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷaippōl iṉṉum anēkam pēr viḻuntumiruk kiṟārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ puttakattil ēḻām, eṭṭām pakkaṅkaḷil koṭut tirukkum aṭṭavaṇaiyaiyum, Mr.Deval eḻutiya puttakattiṉ D. aṭṭavaṇai yaiyum kavaṉittāl cama aḷavuḷḷateṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collum curaṅkaḷ vēṟu oḻuṅkaṟṟa ōcaikaḷuṭaiya curaṅkaḷ vēṟu eṉṟu collukiṟatākak kāṇkiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ collum curaṅkaḷē oḻuṅkaṟṟavai. nāṉ eṉṉa colliyum taṅkaḷ piṭivātattai viṭa māṭṭēṉ eṉṟu cātittāl nāṉ eṉṉa ceyvēṉ. aṉpuḷḷa turaiyē! tāṅkaḷ camīpattiliruntāl veku cīkkirattil camamāṉa aḷavuṭaiya curaṅkaḷiṉ kāṉattiṉ perumaiyaiyum, taṟkālam karnāṭaka caṅkītattiṉ aṉupavattaiyum immuṟaiyē pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ vaḻaṅki vantirukkiṟārkaḷ eṉṟa mēṟkōḷaiyum nāṉ kāṭṭit teḷiya vaittiruppēṉ. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta ratṉākararuṭaiya ca-pa, ca-ma muṟaikaḷaip paṟṟi 13, 9 curutikaḷuḷḷavaiyeṉṟu aṭiyil varum vākkiyattil collukiṟīrkaḷ.

“Verse 51:- Samvadi Svaras are those between which are eight or twelve Srutis.”
“taṅkaḷukkiṭaiyē eṭṭu allatu 12 curaṅkaḷuḷḷavai camvātip porutta curaṅkaḷām.”
“It will be noted that to have eight or twelve Srutis between, means intervals of nine and thirteen Srutis respectively.”
“iṭaiyil 8 allatu 12 curutikaḷuṭaiyavaiyeṉṟu collumpōtu 9 allatu 13 iṭaiveḷikaḷuḷḷa curutikaḷ eṉṟu tāṟpariyam.”

caṅkīta ratṉākarar collum alaku muṟaiyil ēḻāvatu variyiluḷḷa ca-pa vukku 13 alakukaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa. appaṭiyē 2, 4, 5, 6 eṉṟa varikaḷum 13 ākavē varukiṉṟaṉa. āṉāl mutal variyiluḷḷa pa-ri 12 alakākavum 3-āvatu variyiluḷḷa ta-ka II alakākavum varukiṟatē. ivaikaḷ eppaṭip poruntum? tāṅkaḷ koñcam kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl ca-pa viṉ poruttam kiṭaikkāta oru muṟaiyaic coṉṉār eṉṟu teḷivākak kāṇpīrkaḷ. iṉṉum iraṇṭu curutikaḷ cērntāl māttiram ca-pa poruntumeṉṟu teḷivākat terikiṟatu. mummūṉṟāka varum iraṇṭu curaṅkaḷil ov voṉṟu cērttuc colla vēṇṭum.
ippaṭiyē oṉpatu curutiyuṭaiya ca-ma poruttamum oṉpatu, oṉpatāy vara vēṇṭiyataṟkup patil pattum patiṉoṉṟumāka varukiṟatu. ivaikaḷaik kavaṉikkāmal 22 curutiyai viḻuṅki 25 curutiyai ēppamiṭukiṟīrkaḷ. pūrva tamiḻmakkaḷ vaḻaṅki vanta 24 curutikaḷil iraṇṭu alaku kuṟaittuk kamakamāyp pāṭavēṇṭumeṉṟa cūṭcumattai aṟiyāmal parataraiyum caṅkīta ratṉākararaiyum uyarnta pīṭattil vaikkiṟīrkaḷ.
tāṅkaḷ pūrva tamiḻ nūl muṟaikaḷaip pārkkāta kuṟaiyē yoḻiya vēṟillai. ātiyōṭan tamāyt teḷivākac collum nūlkaḷillāmai yiṉāl tamiḻ nāṭṭilullōrum 22 eṉṟu cātikka ārampittārkaḷ. tuvāvimcati curutiyiṉ mayakkam koṇṭa caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷ muṉ oṉṟum piṉ oṉṟumākap pēcik kutarkkam ceytārkaḷ. eṉṟālum vivēkikaḷ uṇmaiyaiyum aṉupōkattaiyum aṟintu tairiyappaṭut tiṉārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ ōcaikaḷ ēṇiyaippōla cama aḷavuṭaiyavaikaḷā yirukkavēṇṭumeṉṟu muṟaippaṭiyē nāṉ kaṇitattilum, aṉupōkattilum kāṭṭiṉēṉ. itaṟku mēlum tāṅkaḷ aṟiyāmaliruppatu eṉ atiruṣṭan tāṉ.
7. itōṭu tāṅkaḷ collum ārmōṉik iṭaiveḷikaḷaip paṟṟi caṟṟup pārppōm.
(1) inta ārmōṉik iṭaiveḷikaḷaip paratarum caṅkīta ratṉākararum kaṉavilum kaṇṭiruppatillai.
(2) ca-pa 2/3, ca-ma 3/4 eṉṟa aḷavai avarkaḷ curam kaṇṭupiṭippataṟku nūlkaḷil collavumillai.
(3) ca-pa 13 curutikaḷaiyuṭaiyavai ca-ma 9 curutikaḷaiyuṭaiyavaiyeṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷē yoḻiya 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟu collavillai.
(4) avar muṟaippaṭi ca-pa 709 ceṉṭskaḷākavum ca-ma 491 ceṉṭs kaḷākavum varukiṉṟaṉa. itaṟkum 702 ceṉṭskaḷāy varum 2/3 kkum 498 ceṉṭskaḷāka varum 3/4kkum eṉṉa campantamirukkiṟatu? itai uṟṟup pārkkāmal Harmonic Ratio eṉṟu caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷukkut teriyāta kaṇakkukaḷaic collukiṟīrkaḷ. intak kaṇakkilēyā caṅkītam irukkiṟatu? ikkaṇakku maṟṟavarukkut teriyāteṉṟu parikācamum paṇṇukiṟīrkaḷ.
pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷākap paramparaiyāyt tamiḻ makkaḷ pāṭik koṇṭirukkum caṅkītattaik kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl patiṉmūṉṟu oṉpatu eṉṟa muṟaiyum aṅku illai. 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa puraḷiyum aṅku illai. pa 2/3, ma 3/4, ka5/6 mutaliya piṉṉaṅkaḷai eṭuttuk koṇṭu avaikaḷai oṉṟōṭoṉṟu perukki varum eṇkaḷai iṅkē colkiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ collukiṟa piṉṉak kaṇakku cariyallavē. āṉāl muṉṉuḷḷa periyōrkaḷ ippaṭic collavillai. atāvatu ca-pa, ca-pa vāka oru stāyiyil 12 curaṅkaḷ varum eṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷ. avarōkaṇa muṟaiyāy ca-ma, ca-ma vāka oru stāyiyil 12 curaṅkaḷum varukiṉṟaṉa veṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷē yoḻiya 2/3 āl cila curaṅkaḷaiyum, 3/4 āl cila curaṅkaḷaiyum, 5/6 āl cila curaṅkaḷaiyum, kaṇṭupiṭikkac coṉṉārkaḷā? 2/3, 2/3 ākap perukki oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷait tāṅkaḷ kaṇṭu piṭittāl appōtu varumpiṉṉa eṇkaḷiṉ viparītam taṅkaḷukkut teriyum. ippiṉṉaṅkaḷukkum 13, 9, 4, 3, 2, 1 eṉṟa caṅkīta ratṉākarariṉ ilakkaṅ kaḷukkum evvita campantamumillai. ivaikaḷaippaṟṟit tāṅkaḷ collukiṟatu pōla āṭamparamāka nāṉ collalām. āṉāl nāṉ colvatait teḷivākat tāṅkaḷ aṟintu koṇṭu maṉantiruntuvataṟku ēṟṟa aḷavu māttiram coṉṉēṉ. taṅkaḷukku ivai pōtāteṉṟāl iṉṉa iṉṉa viṣayam eṉṟu kuṟittu eḻutuṅkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ tiruptiyākum varaikkum uṇmaiyāṉavaikaḷai eḻuta mikap piriyamāyirukkiṟēṉ. uṇmaiyaṟṟavaikaḷai nāṉ eḻuta virumpavillai. nāṉ ārāyntu pārkkāta oṉṟaiyumtaṅkaḷukku eḻuta māṭṭēṉ. tāṅkaḷ intiya caṅkītattai vicārikkat tuvaṅkum poḻutē ‘varaiyāṭṭuk kuṭṭikaḷiṉ kālmoḻikaḷaip puraṭṭiviṭṭu vaḷartta rāpiṉcaṉ kurucōvaippōl’ tappitamāṉa kaṇakkiṉāl vēṟu oru ticaikkut taṅkaḷai tiruppi viṭṭārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ cellum kōṇalāṉa vaḻiyai viṭṭu oḻuṅkāṉa pātaikkut tirumpuṅkaḷ. tirumpuṅkaḷ eṉṟu mikavum kēṭṭuk koḷḷu kiṟēṉ. ‘muḷḷil utaippatu uṉakku kaṭiṉamām’ eṉṟu cuvāmi collum paṭi naṭanta muraṭṭuc cavultāṉē maṉan tiruntiyapiṉ paricutta pavul appōstalaṉāṉār.
21. “curukkamāka eṉ apippirāyam eṉṉa veṉṟāl taṟkālam varai Artificial caṅkītamāṉatu āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷaikaḷil iruntatē yallāmal nicamāy upayōkattilillai eṉpatē.”
mēṟkāṭṭiya kuṟippiṉāl cama aḷavāṉa iṭaiveḷikaḷaiyuṭaiya caṅkītam āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷaiyil iruntatēyallāmal uṇmai yāy upayōkattil illai eṉkiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷaikaḷaip pārttirukkiṟatākac collukiṟīrkaḷ. epṭip pārttīrkaḷō eṉṟu nāṉ āccariyappaṭukiṟēṉ. pīraṅkiyiṉ iruppuk kuṇṭukaḷaip pōla eppakkattilum kaṉatta ōṭukaḷiṉāl mūṭappaṭṭuḷḷa mūḷaikaḷ taṅkaḷukku ilakuvāka eppaṭit terintaṉa? vāyiṉāl nāḷatu varaiyum tamiḻ makkaḷ pāṭikkoṇṭirukkum kītam iṉṉateṉṟu aṟintukoḷvatu mikac culapa meṉṟu eṇṇukiṟēṉ. aṉupōkattilikkum icculapamāṉa muṟaiyait terintu koḷḷātirukkiṟa tāṅkaḷ, kaṇṇukkup pulappaṭātirukkum mūḷaikkuṭ pōy eppaṭik kaṇṭupiṭittīrkaḷ?
oru vēḷai tāṅkaḷ mūḷai eṉṟu colvatai avarkaḷ eḻutiya nūliṉ karutteṉṟu collukiṟatāka vaittukkoṇṭāl, tamiḻ icai nūlkaḷ taṅkaḷukkut teriyātē. avaikaḷiṉ karuttai itu varaiyilu muḷḷa tamiḻmakkaḷum caṅkīta ratṉākararum ataṉ muṉ paratarum cariyāy aṟintu koḷḷātirukkaiyil tāṅkaḷ aṟintukoṇṭatu eppaṭi, curaṅkaḷum curutikaḷum cama aḷavuṭaiyavaikaḷāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu avarkaḷ coṉṉārkaḷ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷum ‘curamum curutiyum cama iṭaiveḷikaḷuṭaiyatāy vara vēṇṭum. ca-pa, ca-ma muṟaiyāy curaṅkaḷ kaṇṭupiṭikkappaṭa vēṇṭumeṉṟa pūrvattāriṉ muṟaippaṭiyē cura varicaikaḷ cama aḷavuṭaiyavaikaḷāyirukkum. avaikaḷ ēṇippaḻuvaip pōla ēṟutaṟkum iṟaṅkutaṟkum aṉukūlamāyirukka vēṇṭum’ eṉṟu tiṣṭāntam colli eccarittum irukkiṟīrkaḷ. āṉāl taṅkaḷ mūḷaiyi liruntapaṭi aṉupōkattiṟku varavillaiyē. oḻuṅkīṉamāṉa iṭaiveḷi kaḷaiyuṭaiya 25 curutikaḷait tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ. avaikaḷai itaṉ muṉ pārttirukkiṟōm. uṇmai taṅkaḷ talaiyil iruntirukkiṟatu. kaiyil vantatō apattam. itai aṉupōkattilirukkum curaṅkaḷukku ottuvaravillaiyeṉṟu āl intiya mīyūcik kāṉpareṉsil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷ kaṇṭu taḷḷiṉārkaḷē. piṉṉai ēṉ tāṅkaḷ maṟṟavarkaḷaip paḻikka vēṇṭum? col oṉṟum ceykai vēṟumāyiruntāl ulakam aruvarukkumē.
pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ curutikaḷ camamāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu tāṅkaḷ niṉaittavaikaḷaiyē coṉṉārkaḷ. coṉṉavaikaḷaiyē cātittuk kāṭṭi yirukkiṟārkaḷ. avarkaḷ kāṭṭiyapaṭiyē nāḷatu varaiyum aṉupōkamu mirukkiṟatu. ivaikaḷait terintu koḷvataṟku muṉ nāṉum taṅkaḷaip pōlavē kalaṅkiṉēṉ. āṉāl taṅkaḷaippōl pustakamum ārmōṉiya mum ceytukoḷḷavillai. iravu pakal itē niṉaivāyiruntu vēlai ceytu koṇṭu varukaiyil teyvātīṉamāy iraṇṭu, mūṉṟu kuṟippukaḷ terintu avaikaḷ aṉupōkattukku vantaṉa. aṉupōkattiṟku vantirunta taṉāl tamiḻ nūliṟ colliya viṣayaṅkaḷai aṟintu koḷḷak kūṭiya vaṉāṉēṉ. illaiyāṉāl nāṉum taṅkaḷaip pōliruppēṉ. oru stāyiyil 24 curutikaḷ irukkiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu aṟinta nāṉ oru irāka cañcārattiṟkuriya pūraṇa amcaṅkaḷaiyum kāṭṭakkūṭiya kītam eḻutavum, avaikaḷil kīrttaṉam uṇṭākkavum kūṭiya tiṟamaiyaiyaṭaintēṉ. avaikaḷaic ceytu kāṭṭa nōkkamuṭaiyavaṉāy aṅku vantēṉ. tāṅkaḷ curutiyaip paṟṟi vātāṭum camayattil capaiyōr koṭutta oru ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇattil oru kīrttaṉamāvatu irākac cāyaiyāvatu putitākac ceytu pāṭik kāṭṭumpaṭi uṅkaḷaik kēṭka vēṇṭumeṉṟu piraciṭeṇṭ navāp ālikkāṉ avarkaḷukkuk kaṭitattil eḻuti ñāpakappaṭuttiṉēṉ. āṉāl avarkaḷ ‘itu yārāl muṭiyum?’ eṉṟu taṅkaḷaik kēṭkāmal niṟutti viṭṭārkaḷ.
nāṉō tāṅkaḷ koṭukkum ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇattil irāka cañcāramāvatu, kītamāvatu, kīrttaṉamāvatu ceyyat tayarāy vantiruntēṉ. nāṉ eṉṉaip perumaiyāyc collik koḷvatu cariyalla. āyiṉum eṉṉaip paṟṟi muṟṟilum teriyāta taṅkaḷukkuc cila kuṟippukaḷaic colvatu tappitamākātu. nāṉ karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅki varum curam curutikaḷ iṉṉavaiyeṉṟum iṉṉiṉṉa curutikaḷ iṉṉiṉṉa kīrttaṉaṅ kaḷōṭu varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟum kaṇṭupiṭitta piṉ tamiḻ nūlil itaṉ viparam aṟintēṉ. appaṭiyē kītam ceyvataṟkum kīrttaṉaṅkaḷ ceyvataṟ kumuriya muṟai terinta piṉpē pūrva tamiḻ nūlkaḷil avaikaḷ collap paṭṭirukkiṉṟaṉa eṉṟu kaṇṭēṉ. ivaikaḷ yāvum irākaṅkaḷaip paṟṟic collum iraṇṭām puttakattil viparamāy veḷi varum. nāṉ kaṇṭu piṭittēṉ eṉṟa perumai pārāṭṭik koḷvataip pārkkilum ivaikaḷuk kuriya ātāramāṉa vitivakaikaḷ pūrva tamiḻ nūlkaḷil kāṇappaṭuvataṉāl avaikaḷaiyē eṉakku ātāramāka eṭuttukkoṇṭēṉ. nāṉ eṭuttuk koṇṭa viṣayattil tamiḻ nūlkaḷ mūlamāyt teyvam ivvaḷavāvatu kirupai ceytārē yeṉṟu mikunta cantōṣamaṭaintēṉ.
atōṭu eṉṉaic cantikkum tērnta vitvāṉkaḷ palarukkum kītam paṭittukkāṭṭi oppukkoḷḷappaṭṭirukkiṟatu. maicūr camastāṉa vitvāṉ vaiṇīka cikāmaṇi makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cēṣaṇṇā avarkaḷum, vijayanakaram camastāṉa vitvāṉ vaiṇīka cirōmaṇi makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi vēṅkaṭa ramaṇatās avarkaḷum, arikēcavanallūr, makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi muttaiyāya pākavatar avarkaḷum, tañcai, vīṇai vēṅkaṭācalamaiyar avarkaḷum kīta muṟaikaḷaik kēṭṭu mikavum cantōṣattuṭaṉ oppuk koṇṭirukkiṟārkaḷ. kīta muṟaikaḷaik kēṭṭuc cantōṣamaṭainta maicūr, makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi kiruṣṇa rāv B.A. avarkaḷiṉ apippirāyattai aṭiyil varum cila varikaḷil kāṇka.
Indian Music Journal By H.P.Krishna Rao, B.A. Vol.I. No.5. 191, Page 102, 103.
“Two days-25th and 26th were spent at Tanjore in the company of Rao Sahib Abraham Pandither avl. The Rao Sahib is a very popular gentleman both by his profession and good nature. He is an ardent admirer of music and the treatise on music that he is writing is likely to be of immense good to the students only if he would carry out the plans he has chalked out. All his children are well-versed in music, eastern and well as western, and it is a great pleasure to every friend of the Pandit to listen to the sweet singing of his children in solo or in concert. One admirable work that he is engaged in is the laying down of a set of rules for enabling every student of music to compose Gitams, Swarajatis and other Pieces.
makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi II, P. kiruṣṇarāv B.A. avarkaḷuṭaiya intiyaṉ miyūcik jarṉal Vol.I. No.5.  1911 pakkam 102, 103.
“25 ām, 26 ām tētikaḷākiya iraṇṭu nāṭkaḷaiyum tañcāvūril Rao Sahib Pandither avarkaḷuṭaṉ kaḻittōm. taṉṉuṭaiya toḻil mūlamāyum caṟkuṇattiṉ mūlamāyum Rao Sahib avarkaḷ yāvarālum naṉku matikkap paṭṭārkaḷ. caṅkītattil avarkaḷukku attiyanta pirīti. ippōtu avarkaḷ eḻutik koṇṭu varum caṅkīta nūlāṉatu avarkaḷ maṉatil niṉaittiruk kiṟa piḷāṉpaṭi muṭivaṭaiyumāṉāl caṅkītam paṭippavarkaḷukku atika pirayōcaṉamuḷḷatāy irukkum. avarkaḷ kumārar kumārattikaḷ ellārum mēṟṟicai caṅkītattilum kīḻtticai caṅkītattilum tērntavarkaḷāṉatāl avarkaḷ iṉṉicaiyōṭu taṉittup pāṭuvataiyum ellōrum oṉṟu cērntu pāṭuvataiyum avarkaḷ cinēkitarellōrum kēṭṭu āṉantikkum paṭiyāṉa cilākkiyam irukkiṟatu. ippōtu avarkaḷ ceytu varum vēlai yiṉ arumaiyāṉa pākam eṉṉaveṉṟāl caṅkītam kaṟkum ovvoru varum tāṉāy kītam, svarajati mutaliyavaṟṟai eḻutum paṭikkāṉa vitikaḷai eḻutikkoṇṭu varuvatē.”
itaṉ arumaiyai mutal mutal tamiḻ makkaḷum ataṉpiṉ maṟṟavarum veku cīkkiram aṟivārkaḷ. eṉ niṉaippiliruntataiyē vāyiṉāl coṉṉēṉ. kaiyiṉāl ceytu kāṭṭiṉēṉ. piḷḷaikaḷ pāṭiṉārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ ca-pa muṟaiyāka varum curaṅkaḷ cama iṭaiveḷikaḷuṭaiyavaikaḷāyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu colvatum, ēṇip paḻukkaḷaip pōl ēṟutaṟkum, iṟaṅkutaṟkum utaviyāyirukka vēṇṭu meṉṟu colvataṟkup poruntuvatum, aṉupōkattukku varakkūṭiyatum, pallāyira varuṭaṅkaḷākat tamiḻ makkaḷ pāṭikkoṇṭiruppatum ivaikaḷē. ivaikaḷaittāṉē āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷaiyiliruntavai eṉṟum taṅkaḷ mūḷaiyil iruppavai eṉṟum tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ.
itait tāṅkaḷ artificial iṭaiveḷikaḷuṭaiya teṉṟu ēḷaṉañ ceykiṟīrkaḷ. oṉṟāyirunta ātāra caṭcam paṭippaṭiyāy mēlē pōkum poḻutu mattiyastāyi caṭcam iraṇṭākavum ataṉ mēl tāra caṭcam pōkum poḻutu nālākavum varum eṉṟa caṅkīta ratṉākarariṉ vacaṉam Geometrical Progression aittāṉ kuṟikkum eṉṟu aṟivāḷikaḷ oppuk koḷvārkaḷē. ataṉ irakaciyam taṅkaḷukku itaṉmuṉ terintiruntāl itai artificial eṉṟu colliyirukkamāṭṭīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷ pustakam 34 ām pakkattil oru stāyiyai iraṇṭākavum mūṉṟāvum paṉṉiraṇṭākavum pirippataṟku lākarta muṟaippaṭiyirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu mika aṟpamākat taṅkaḷukkut tōṉṟiyirukkiṟatu. eṉṟālum atu ‘kuruṭaṉ taṉ kālil taṭṭiya paṇappaiyaik kalleṉṟu niṉaittuk kālāl taḷḷiviṭṭu appuṟam pōṉatu pōl’ uṅkaḷait tavaṟutalāka naṭatta ētuvāyiruntatē yoḻiya cariyāṉa muṟaikku vaḻi naṭattavillai. cariyāṉa muṟaiyākac collum cila mēṟṟicaiyāriṉ nūlkaḷaiyum tāṅkaḷ pārkkavillai pōlirukkiṟatu.
The art of tuning the Pianoforte by Hermann Smith, Page. 75, 76.
“Mr.W.H.B.Woolhouse remarks truly, “It is very misleading to suppose that the necessity of temperament applies only to instruments which have fixed tones. Singers and performers on perfect instruments must all temper their intervals, or they could not keep in tune with each other, or even with themselves; and on arriving at the same notes by different routes would be continually finding a want of agreement. The scale of Equal temperament obviates all such inconveniences, and continues to be universally accepted with unqualified satisfaction by the most eminent vocalists; and equally so by the most renowned and accomplished performers on stringed instruments, although these instruments are capable of an infinite variety of intonation. The high development of modern instrumentl Music would not have been possible, and could not have been acquired, without the manifold advantages of the tempered intonation by equal semitones, and it has, in consequence, long become the established basis of tunning.”
“Mr.Woolhouse eṉpavar eṉṉa collukiṟār eṉṟāl, curaṅkaḷ stāpamāyirukkappaṭṭa vāttiyaṅkaḷukkuttāṉ curaṅkaḷukkuc caripākamāyp pirikkummuṟai avaciyam, maṟṟavaikaḷukku avaciyamalla eṉṟu niṉaippatu picaku. pūraṇavāttiyaṅkaḷai vaittup pāṭupavarkaḷum, vācippavarkaḷum kūṭa taṅkaḷ curaṅkaḷaic curutikkēṟka amaittuk koḷḷāviṭṭāl, maṟṟavarkaḷōṭu cērntu pāṭavāvatu tāṅkaḷē cutta curattil pāṭavāvatu kūṭātu. pala vaḻikaḷiṉ mūlamāy orē curaṅkaḷil vantu cēravēṇṭiya avaciyam iruppatāl aṭikkaṭi vācippōrukkum pāṭuvōrukkum cura vittiyācaṅkaḷ ēṟpaṭṭuk koṇṭēyirukkakkūṭiyatu. curutikaḷai camapākamākap pirittu stāpikkappaṭṭa ārōkaṇamāṉatu ivvita vittiyā caṅkaḷai uṇṭākka māṭṭātu. atuvē caṅkītam pāṭukiṟa vitvāṉkaḷ muṟai. vāttiyaṅkaḷ palavum palavitamāy curutiyēṟṟak kūṭiyavaiyā yirunta pōtilum tantivāttiyaṅkaḷil nipuṇarāṉa ellā caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum cariyeṉṟu oppukkoḷḷum vaḻiyum ituvē. ippaṭi curaṅkaḷukkiṭaiyiluḷḷa iṭaiveḷikaḷai camapākaṅkaḷākap pirikkum muṟai ēṟpaṭṭapiṟakutāṉ, caṅkīta vāttiyakāṉamāṉatu atika tērcciyaṭain tirukkiṟatu mallāmal, atuvē ellā vāttiyaṅkaḷaiyum curutikkēṟkak koṇṭuvarum muṟaiyeṉṟum, atiṉāl uṇṭākum pirayōcaṉaṅkaḷ aṉantam eṉṟum, yāvarālum oppukkoḷḷappaṭukiṟatu.”

cākruṭīṉ cāyapu nuṭpamāṉa curaṅkaḷaip pakuttaṟiyak kūṭiya kātuṭaiyavaralla eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. eṉṉiṭattil avaraippaṟṟit tāṅkaḷ colla eṉṉa avaciyamirukkiṟatu? eppoḻutu avar vāyait tiṟantu taṉṉāl kūṭiya atikanēram orē curutiyil curattaic coṉṉārō appoḻutē avar takunta vitvāṉ eṉṟu nāṉ eṇṇiṉēṉ. avar taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ curam cariyāyirukkiṟatō illaiyō eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ pala taṭavai pārkkum varaiyilum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ apacuram taṉ kātiṟpukāmal kaiyaik kātil vaittuk koṇṭu oru curattilēyē alaivillāmalum kūṭutal kuṟaivillāmalum niṉṟār. tāṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattiṉ kāṟṟāṭiyaip palamāka mitittum cura stāṉattaip palamāka aḻuttiyum Major tone-kkum Minor tonekkum māṟṟi māṟṟip pārttīrkaḷ. 25 curuti varicaiyil etaiyāvatu piṭittuk kāṭṭi viṭalāmeṉṟu pala nimiṣam pirayattaṉappaṭṭīrkaḷ. āṉāl avarō mikunta kāmpīramāy muṉ piṉ pōkāmal oru curattilēyē niṉṟu kāṭṭiṉār. ippaṭik kāṭṭiṉa oru vitvāṉai atika curañāṉam uḷḷavar eṉṟu collat tayārāyillai eṉkiṟīrkaḷ. yār uṅkaḷait tērnta vitvāṉ eṉṟu collumpaṭik kēṭṭārkaḷ? piḷḷaikaḷ vīṇaiyil 24 curutikaḷaip pāṭik kāṭṭukaiyil atōṭu avarum cērntu 24 curutikaḷai vāyiṉāl pāṭikkāṭṭiṉārē. atait tāṅkaḷum kēṭṭuk koṇṭiruntīrkaḷ. appaṭip paṭṭa oruvarai curaṅkaḷaip pakuttaṟiyakkūṭiya kātuṭaiyavaralla eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷē, itu niyāyamā yirukkiṟatā? maṟṟavarkaḷ tāṅkaḷ colvatai oppukkoḷvārkaḷā?
tāṅkaḷ intustāṉi irākaṅkaḷil vaḻaṅki varum curaṅkaḷukku ottuvarāta ārmōṉiyam ceytu vantatiṉāl intustāṉi caṅkītatti lāvatu, piḷḷaikaḷ pāṭiyapoḻutu ‘vēṟu ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇaṅkaḷukku māṟip pōṉārkaḷ’ eṉṟu colvatiṉāl karnāṭaka caṅkītattilāvatu, curaṅkaḷ cama aḷavuṭaiyatāy ēṇip paḻuvaippōl varavēṇṭumeṉṟu colliviṭṭu ‘paṇṭitar Equal Temperament muṟaikku iḻukkiṟār, piḷḷaikaḷ artificial iṭaiveḷikaḷai upayōkippatiṉāl kāṉam aruvaruppāyiruntatu’ eṉṟu colvatiṉāl iṅkilīṣ miyūcikkilāvatu taṅkaḷukkut takunta ñāṉamillai eṉṟu teḷivākak kāṭṭukiṟīrkaḷ. immūṉṟu vitamāṉa caṅkītamum teriyāta tāṅkaḷ cākruṭīṉ cāyapu avarkaḷai niyāyantīrppatu eppaṭi? atai yār oppukkoḷvārkaḷ? taṅkattukkum korintu tēcattiṉ pittaḷaikkum pētamillaiyā?
avaraip paṟṟic colvatu taṅkaḷ mēl kuṟṟamillai. tāṅkaḷ 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa cura ñāṉa maṟṟavarkaḷ collum kaṇakkai eṭuttukkoṇṭu kaṇṭupiṭikkum oḻuṅkaṟṟa curuti muṟaiyaic collik kāṭṭum ārmōṉiyattai nāṅkaḷ pārttum atiluḷḷa apacuraṅkaḷaik kēṭṭu mirukkiṟōm. apacurak kuṭukkaiyākiya av ārmōṉiyattiṉāl uṅkaḷ kātu keṭṭuppōyirukkiṟatu. ellōrum mikunta piriyamāy periya vitvāṉ eṉṟu koṇṭāṭi rājacapaiyilum pāṭumpaṭic ceyta avarai mikat tērnta vitvāṉ alla eṉṟu colvataṟkuk kāraṇam intiya caṅkītattil taṅkaḷukku irukkum kuṟainta aṟivē eṉṟu eṇṇukiṟēṉ. capaiyōr yāvaraiyum āṉantikkac ceyta kuḻantaikaḷiṉ kāṉam taṅkaḷai māttiram aruvarukkac ceyta kāraṇam yātu? taṅkaḷiṉ ārmōṉiyattil varum apacuramallavā? palavita puṣpaṅkaḷaik kaṭṭum pūkkaṭṭi vīṭṭut tiṇṇaiyil, irāttiri paṭuttirukka vēṇṭumeṉṟu uttiravu kēṭṭup paṭuttirunta vaḻippōkkarāṉa mīṉ viyāpārikaḷ, puṣpa vācaṉaiyiṉāl tūkkam varāmal neṭunēram puraṇṭu puraṇṭu caṅkaṭappaṭṭup piṉpu taṅkaḷ mīṉ kūṭaiyai eṭuttut talaiyil kaviḻttuk koṇṭu naṉṟāyt tūṅkiṉārkaḷ eṉpatupōla, apacuram niṟainta ārmōṉiyam taṅkaḷ kātai evvaḷavākak keṭuttirukkiṟateṉṟu aṟintu, itaṟkup parikāramillaiyō eṉṟu varuttappaṭukiṟēṉ.
itōṭu tāṅkaḷ collum cila pariṭcaikaḷum cila irākaṅkaḷil varum curaṅkaḷiṉ tīrmāṉamum 2/3, 3/4 eṉṟa aḷaviṉāl tāṅkaḷ kaṇṭu colvataik koṇṭu avaikaḷaip paṟṟi nāṉ colvatu vīṇvēlai yākum eṉṟu viṭṭuviṭṭēṉ.

eṉ maṉatiṟkut taṅkaḷ viyācattaip pārttavuṭaṉ mika aruvaruppā yiruntatu. eṉṟālum eṉ maṉatai camātāṉappaṭuttikkoṇṭu cila kuṟippukaḷ eḻutiṉēṉ.

atāvatu :-
1. ‘parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil enta vitamāṉa rucuvum carivara naṭattappaṭavillai’ eṉpataṉāl āl intiya miyūcik capaiyaip paṟṟik kuṟaivākavum, 										(3)
2. ‘ārmōṉiyattaippaṟṟi naṭanta pariṣaiyāṉatu parikācak kūttāyiruntatu’ eṉpataṉāl capaiyil vantiruntavarkaḷ ataippariṭcikkat takuntavarkaḷ alla eṉṟum, 								(4)
3. ‘capaiyil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷ Major tone, Minor tone, Tempered Scale mutaliya nuṭpamāṉa vittiyācaṅkaḷait teriyātavarkaḷ. āṉāl piṉṉa eṇkaḷait taṅkaḷukkut teriyāmalē upayōkikkiṟārkaḷ’ eṉpatiṉāl capaiyil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷ caṅkītamāvatu, kaṇitamāvatu uṅkaḷaip pōl teriyātavarkaḷ eṉṟum, 						(6)
4. ‘piḷḷaikaḷ pāṭiyatu uṅkaḷ apippirāyattai nilainiṟuttiṉatāka niṉaikkiṟīrkaḷ’ eṉpataṉāl eṉ apippirāyam vēṟu piḷḷaikaḷiṉ kāṉam vēṟāyiruntateṉṟum, 									(7)
5. ‘tampurāvai vaittup pāṭātataṉāl avarkaḷ cariyāṉa caṅkītam pāṭavillai’ eṉpataṉāl avarkaḷ tappāṉa caṅkītam pāṭiṉārkaḷ eṉṟum, 													(8)
6. ‘Artificial iṭaiveḷikaḷai upayōkittataṉāl aruvaruppāyiruntatu. iṉimaiyāyillai, vēṟu ārōkaṇa avarōkaṇaṅkaḷukku māṟi viṭṭārkaḷ’ eṉṟu colvataṉāl piḷḷaikaḷ pāṭiya pāṭalkaḷ muṟṟum tavaṟutaleṉṟum, 									(9, 11, 12, 13)
7. ‘curaṅkaḷ cama aḷavuṭaiyatāyp pirikka vēṇṭumeṉṟa cāsti rōktamillāta oru caṅkīta muṟaiyai ēṟpaṭuttiṉārkaḷ’ eṉṟu colvataṉāl cama aḷavāyp piritta pūrva tamiḻ muṉivarkaḷaiyum eṉṉaiyum payittiyakkārarkaḷeṉṟum, 						(19)
8. ‘Artificial caṅkītamāṉatu āti cāstirikaḷiṉ mūḷaiyi liruntatē yallāmal upayōkattilillai’ eṉpataṉāl avarkaḷ aṉupōka maṟṟavarkaḷ eṉṟum, vīṇāṉa cāstiraṅkaḷai eḻuti vaittārkaḷeṉṟum, 													(21)
9. ‘capaiyil vantiruntavarkaḷ taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattai aruvaruttu appiriyappaṭṭārkaḷ’ eṉpataṉāl avarkaḷ pārapaṭcamuḷḷavarkaḷeṉṟum niyāyantīrkkan takutiyaṟṟavarkaḷ eṉṟum,					 (22)
10. ‘cākruṭīṉ cāyapu atiṉāl iḻukkappaṭṭār’ eṉṟu colvataṉāl avar oru nilaiyil nilaittirāta pattāmpacali cōṭāpāṭṭilaip pōla niccaya puttiyillātava reṉṟum. 							(22)
11. ‘cākruṭīṉ cāyapu atika nuṭpamāṉa kātuṭaiyavareṉṟu collat tayārāyillai’yeṉṟu tāṅkaḷ colvataṉāl avarukku caṅkītat tiṟamai pōtātu eṉṟum collukiṟīrkaḷ. 						(24)
ivviṣayaṅkaḷait tāṅkaḷ naṉṟāyk kavaṉittup pārttīrkaḷāṉāl ikkuṟippukaḷil enta oṉṟaiyāvatu colla muṟṟilum takutiyaṟṟavarkaḷ eṉṟu tōṉṟum, āyiṉum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭataṉāl uṇṭākiya maṉa varuttattiṉālum - maṉakkuḻappattiṉālum - paṇac celaviṉālum - avamāṉattiṉālum ippaṭic collukiṟīrkaḷ eṉṟu eṉṉaic cāntappaṭuttikkoṇṭu itai eḻutiṉēṉ.
tāṅkaḷ oppukkoḷḷum mukkiyamāṉa iraṇṭu kuṟippukaḷ.
(1) ‘karakarappiriyā irākattil varum curaṅkaḷukku ārmōṉiyam kuṟaintateṉṟu cākruṭīṉ cāyapu coṉṉār’ eṉṟu colvatum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam capaimuṉ pariṭcikkappaṭṭut taḷḷappaṭṭatu eṉṟa karut taṭaṅkiya vārttaikaḷaic colvatum,
(2) ‘taṅkaḷ kuḻantaikaḷiṉ kāṉam cākruṭīṉālum maṟṟavarkaḷālum atikamāyp pukaḻappaṭṭatu’ (aticayikkappaṭṭatu) eṉṟu colvatum caṟṟu uṇmaiyāyirukkiṉṟatu.
ivviraṇṭaiyum tāṅkaḷ oppukkoṇṭatē pōtum. ivviraṇṭai yum paṟṟiyē muṉ viyācattil eḻutiyiruntēṉ. ippōtum oppuk koḷḷukiṟīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭatum piḷḷaikaḷiṉ kāṉam oppukkoḷḷappaṭṭatum parōṭāvil naṭantavaikaḷil mukkiya māṉavai. ivviraṇṭiṉ campantamāy uṇmaiyāka naṭantavaikaḷai yāvarum aṟintukoḷḷa iṅku eḻutiṉēṉ. ivviraṇṭaiyum tāṅkaḷ oppukkoṇṭa piṉ iṉimēl maṟuttu eḻutap peṉ eṭukkat tuṇiya māṭṭīrkaḷeṉṟu niṉaikkiṟēṉ. ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭatu piḷḷaikaḷiṉ kāṉam yāvarālum atikamākap pukaḻappaṭṭatu (āccariyamāy eṇṇappaṭṭatu) eṉṟu māttiram colliyiruppīrkaḷāṉāl tāṅkaḷ mikunta pukaḻccikku pāttirarāyiruppīrkaḷ. ettaṉai peyaraip puṇpaṭuttiviṭṭīrkaḷ. itu intiya caṅkītattiṟku utaviyalla, upattiravam, upattiravap paṭuttum taṅkaḷaippōl puṇṇiyavāṉkaḷ iṉi oruvarum talaiyeṭukka māṭṭārkaḷ eṉpatu niccayam.
eppaṭiyāvatu taṅkaḷ maṉatil irunta uṇmai veḷivantatu eṉpatai muṭivil aṟiya nāṉ mikavum cantōṣappaṭukiṟēṉ. ivviraṇṭu uṇmai kaḷum taṅkaḷai aṟiyāmalē taṅkaḷ mūḷaiyiliruntu kaivaḻiyāka pēṉāvil iṟaṅki maiyiṉāl kaṭitattil eḻutappaṭṭaṉa. taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷappaṭṭateṉṟum piḷḷaikaḷiṉ kāṉam pukaḻappaṭṭa teṉṟum tāṅkaḷē collum poḻutu nāṉ vēṟu eṉṉa colla irukkiṟatu. uṇmaiyaik kavaṉikkum cila kaṉavāṉkaḷ eḻutiya kaṭitattiṉālum ivaikaḷ pulappaṭukiṉṟaṉa. avaikaḷil iraṇṭoṉṟait tāṅkaḷ pārkka vēṇṭiyatu avaciyam.
parōṭā kāṉpareṉsukku vantiruntavarkaḷil Mr.Bhatkande B.A., L.L.B.,  avarkaḷaiyum maicūr camastāṉam vaiṇīka vitvāṉ Mr.kiruṣṇarāv B.A.avarkaḷaiyum tāṅkaḷ aṟivīrkaḷ. avarkaḷ kāṉpareṉsukku vantiruntapoḻutu kavaṉittavaikaḷaip paṟṟik kaṭitaṅkaḷil eḻutiyavaikaḷ taṅkaḷukkum taṅkaḷaippōl eṉ apippirāyattiṟku virōtamāy vātāṭum cila kōṇalkaḷukkum pirayōcaṉamāyirukkumeṉṟu eṇṇu kiṟēṉ.
V.N.BHATKANDE Esq., B.A., L.L.B.,
Santaram House, Malabar Hill, Bombay.
MY DEAR RAO SAHIB PANDITHER,
It is a practically long time since we separated at Baroda and In think I ought to take up my correspondence with you once more in my own interest. I may sincerely tell you that your great labours and scholarship very nearly stunned me. I shall be always proud of having the privilege of calling you my friend. I may or may not agree with all your views but that will never prevent me from always bearing in mind the fact that you are a great Music scholar. I am so thankful to Dewan Saheb that he brought us together. I shall certainly not fail to derive considerable benefit from your labours. I have to thank you most sincerely for coming to my help in hitting that mischievous sruti harmonium movement on the head in time. It had very nearly turned the heads of serveral of our workers here. Mr. Deval had almost persuaded the educational authorities of this presidency to introduce the Harmonium as a compulsory accompaniment in our schools. But for you I should not have been able to make my poor voice heard. You disposed of Deval’s Sharangdev’s srutis like a miracle.
Your exposition has however brought to light one fact and that is likely a disappoint all the present music enthusiasts here. I am referring to that part of your book where you say or rather point out-that with the exception of the Sa and its octave, none of the intermediate notes of will exactly correspond with any of our modern notes. You go on to say again that all attempt at reviving Sarangadev’s music is bound to be a failure. This conclusion of yours seems to be of tremendous importance.
Yours Sincerely,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.
eṉatu piriyamuḷḷa rāv cākēp paṇṭitaravarkaḷukku,
nām parōṭāvil oruvaraiyoruvar viṭṭup pirintu vekukālamāki viṭṭapaṭiyāl eṉṉuṭaiya cuyakāriyattiṟkākavē nāṉ tirumpa taṅkaḷukku eḻutuvatu avaciyamāyt tōṉṟukiṟatu. caṅkītattiṟkākat tāṅkaḷ ceyta vēlaiyum taṅkaḷ kalvit tiṟamaiyum eṉakku atipiramippai uṇṭu paṇṇiṉa. taṅkaḷai eppōtum eṉ cinēkitareṉṟu aḻaikkum cilākkiya māṉatu eṉakku atika perumai. caṅkīta viṣayamāyt tāṅkaḷ collum apippirāyaṅkaḷai nāṉ cariyeṉṟu oppukkoṇṭālum oppukkoḷḷā viṭṭālum tāṅkaḷ caṅkītattil vitvāṉ eṉkiṟa caṅkatiyāṉatu eppōtum eṉ maṉatil irukkum. nammiruvaruṭaiya cinēkitattiṟkum kāraṇarāyirunta Dewan Saheb avarkaḷukku vantaṉam collukiṟēṉ. taṅkaḷuṭaiya vēlaiyiṉ palaṉiliruntu nāṉ atika payaṉ aṭaivēṉ eṉpataṟkuc cantēkamillai.
takka camayam pārttut tāṅkaḷ eṉakku utaviyāy vantu anēka keṭutikaḷ ceytu vanta curuti ārmōṉiyak koḷkaiyiṉ talaiyai uṭaittataṟkāka atika naṉṟiyaṟitaluḷḷavaṉāyirukkiṟēṉ. caṅkīta viṣayattil iṅku uḻaikkum anēkaruṭaiya irutayattai intac curuti ārmōṉiyam koḷḷai koṇṭu pōyviṭṭatu. Mr. tēvāl avarkaḷ inta rājatāṉiyiluḷḷa paḷḷikkūṭaṅkaḷil intac curuti ārmōṉiyat taik kaṭṭāyamāy upayōkappaṭuttumpaṭi kalācālai atipatikaḷai ēṟak kuṟaiya cammatikkap paṇṇiviṭṭārkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ eṉ utavikku varātiruntatāl eṉṉuṭaiya cattam vaṉāntarattil taṉiyāyk kiṭantu kattukiṟavaṉuṭaiya cattam pōlāyirukkumē. Mr. tēvāl avarkaḷuṭaiya cāraṅkatēva curutikaḷait tāṅkaḷ aṟputamāṉa vitamāy māyttu viṭṭīrkaḷ.
āṉāl, tāṅkaḷ collum apippirāyattil oru vicēṣamāṉatu iṅkirukkum caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷukku mikavum atairiyattai uṇṭākku kiṟatu. ateṉṉaveṉṟāl, cāraṅkatēvar muṟaippaṭi oru stāyiyil ṣaṭjamattaiyum atiṉ eṭṭāvatu curamākiya ṣaṭjamattaiyum tavira naṭuvil varum entac curamāvatu taṟkālattil vaḻaṅkum curaṅkaḷukku ottu varātu eṉṟu colluvatutāṉ. cāraṅkatēvaruṭaiya caṅkītattait tirumpa eṭuttu niṟuttuvatu kūṭātakāriyameṉṟum tāṅkaḷ collukiṟīrkaḷ. inta muṭivāṉa vārttaiyāṉatu atika vicēṣamāṉa oru caṅkati.
taṅkaḷiṉ uṇmaiyuḷḷa,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.
mēṟkaṇṭa kaṭitattiṉāl taṅkaḷ curuti ārmōṉiyam taḷḷap paṭṭateṉṟum tēvāl eṭuttuccoṉṉa cāraṅkatēvaruṭaiya curutikaḷ pirayōjaṉamaṟṟavaikaḷ eṉṟu taḷḷappaṭṭaṉaveṉṟum teḷivākac collukiṟār. nāṉ atikam collavēṇṭiyatillai eṉṟu eṇṇu kiṟēṉ.
SHASTARAM HOUSE, MALABAR HILL,
BOMBAY,
Monday 7th Aug. 16
DEAR RAO SAHIB PANDITHER,
Many many thanks for the copies of your refutation of Mr. Clement’s letters to the Madras Mail as also for the two kind letters accompanying the same. I think I have already told you that I would never cease to admire your great labours and scholarship. If I live long enough I won’t be surprised to find you one of these days mentioned as the great leader of the Southern Music School. *     * 	 *      *     *
Then Sharangadeva was dragged in and became their sheet-anchor. I was not able to effectively dislodge them from that position with that success which you obtained the other day. I frankly admit. * *
(In my travels throughout India) Not a single Pandit could argue the Shruti question with anything like precision. No authorities were ever cited or discussed. Many made attempts to say that some of the Ragas admitted smaller tones than semitones but when pressed to explain and demonstrate with reasons and authorities they backed out. No grantha could be cited as authority for the distribution of the Shrutis, which therefore appeared to be to depend on personal whims. As to the use of the well-known 12 notes there was absolutely no disagreement. 		* 	* 	*	*	*
But I had full confidence in my God. “Commit theyself unto God and trust in Him and He will bring it to pass,” was my motto. Who appealed sincerely to God and did not succeed? God Almighty saw that I was unjustly being swamped away by influential mischief-makers and decided to help me. He inspired H.H. The Gaekwar and his most sympathetic prime minister, the large-hearted Dewan Saheb, to take up my cause. Your great assistance also I ascribe to His inspiration. I take no credit to me for all that happened at the Conference. Mr. Deval and Mr. Clements and their great following collapsed like a pack of cards. The Sanskrit Professors corroborated all my interpretations and falsified Deval’s. I never had a Shruti Theory of my own. I relied upon the 12 notes which were firmly established throughout the country. My contention all through my books was that for popular education in music a system based on the established 12 notes was very convenient and therefore ought to be retained. Of course when the minute Shrutis were unanimously accepted by our scholars and practical experts, I had not the lease objection to bow to their decision. It was naturally a great satisfaction to me that the great Conference came and decided that my contentions were not unreasonable. I shall never be elated with success because I know and honestly believe that it was He that was enacting all that was happening there.
*   *    *   *   *
Your 24 Shrutis theory is really very interesting. If it is duly accepted in the South by the musicians there, I should be the first person to give it a trial in our music.
* 	* 	* 	* 	*
Yours sincerely,
(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE.
piriyamuḷḷa rāv cākēp paṇṭitaravarkaḷukku,
kiḷameṇṭs turai meyilil eḻutiya kaṭitattiṟkut tāṅkaḷ eḻutiya maṟuppum attuṭaṉ aṉpāy aṉuppappaṭṭa taṅkaḷuṭaiya iraṇṭu kaṭitaṅkaḷum kiṭaittaṉa. avaikaḷukkāka anēka vantaṉam collukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayattil paṭṭa pirayācaṅkaḷaiyum taṅkaḷuṭaiya kalvit tiṟamaiyaiyum viyantu koḷḷum viṣayattil nāṉ orukālum calippatillai yeṉṟu nāṉ muṉṉamē taṅkaḷukkut terivittirukkiṟēṉ. kaṭavuḷ eṉakku āyucaik koṭukkum pakṣattil cila varuṣaṅkaḷukkuḷ tāṅkaḷ teṉṉintiya caṅkīta muṟaiyai stāpitta periya makāṉ eṉṟu ulakam oppuk koḷvataik kēṭṭāl āccariyappaṭamāṭṭēṉ.

piṟaku (Mr.Clements, Mr.Deval) cāraṅkatēvaruṭaiya pustakattai ātāramākak koṇṭu avar mēl taṅkaḷ naṅkūrattaip pōṭṭārkaḷ. inta naṅkūrattiliruntu avarkaḷaik kiḷappiviṭa eṉakku atikap pirayācaiyā yiruntapōtilum, tāṅkaḷ avarkaḷaip parōṭā kāṉpareṉcil taṅkaḷ pāykaḷai virittu mutuku kāṭṭi yōṭa aṭittīrkaḷ eṉṟu maṉap pūraṇamāy oppuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ. 	* 	* 	* 	* 	*
(intiyāviṉ pala pākaṅkaḷilum cuṟṟi vantatil) curuti viṣayamāy niyāyātāraṅḷait takunta vitamāy eṭuttup pēcakkūṭiya oru vitvāṉāvatu akappaṭavillai. evarāvatu tāṅkaḷ collukiṟataṟku ātārattai eṭuttuk kāṇpikkak kūṭiyavarkaḷāyillai. anēkar, cila irākaṅkaḷil araic curattaiviṭak kuṟainta curutikaḷ irukkiṉṟaṉa eṉṟu colliyum, avaikaḷai vāyppāṭṭiṉ mūlamāvatu kaṇakkukaḷiṉ mūlamāvatu rucuppaṭuttak kēṭkappaṭṭapōtu piṉ vāṅki viṭṭārkaḷ. oru stāyiyil curaṅkaḷai eppaṭi niravukiṟatu eṉpataṟkuk kirantaṅkaḷiṉ mūlamāy oru rucuvum ēṟpaṭātatāl avarkaḷ taṅkaḷ maṉatiṟkut tōṉṟiyapaṭi niravi vantārkaḷ eṉṟu veḷiyāyiṟṟu. āṉāl yāvarukkum terintirunta 12 curaṅkaḷaip paṟṟi evviṭattilāvatu vittiyācamāṉa apippirāyam ciṟitēṉum kāṇappaṭavillai. 	* 	*	 *	
āṉāl kaṭavuḷiṭattil eṉakku muḻu nampikkaiyiruntatu. “uṉ vaḻikaḷaik kaṭavuḷiṭam oppu vittu avarmēl nampikkaiyāyi.ru avarē uṉ kāriyattai vāykkap paṇṇuvār” eṉpatē nāṉ nampiṉa cattiyam. uṇmaiyāyk kaṭavuḷiṭam taṅkaḷ kāriyattai oppuvittavarkaḷil evar cittipeṟāmaṟ pōṉār? uyarnta pataviyil iruntukoṇṭu viṣamam ceykiṟavarkaḷāl nāṉ eṭutta kāriyattiṟku iṭaiyūṟu uṇṭākiṟateṉṟu aṟinta kaṭavuḷ eṉakku utavi ceyya muṉ vantār. avar H.H.keykvār makārājā avarkaḷ maṉatilum mikunta paccātāpamum peruntaṉmaiyum vāynta avarkaḷ mantiriyākiya Dewan Saheb avarkaḷ maṉatilum pukuntu eṉ kāriyattai eṭuttu niṟuttiṉār. tāṅkaḷ eṉakkuc ceyta pērutaviyum kaṭavuḷiṉ naṭattutaltāṉ. kāṉpareṉcil naṭanta yātoṉṟum eṉ ceyalalla.   *	 *         *         *         	
Mr.tēvālum Mr.kiḷameṇṭsum avarkaḷ kūṭṭamum, ārpāṭṭamum viḷaiyāṭum cīṭṭukaḷāl kaṭṭappaṭṭa oru vīṭu aṭiyōṭu cāyvatupōl viḻuntu cāyntu pōṉārkaḷ. eṉ viyākkiyāṉaṅkaḷ ellām cari yeṉṟum tēvāluṭaiya viyākkiyāṉaṅkaḷellām poyyeṉṟum camas kiruta paṇṭitarkaḷāl uṟuti ceyyappaṭṭatu. nāṉāka curuti muṟai oṉṟum uṇṭākkavillai. tēcameṅkum cātāraṇamāy vaḻaṅkivarum 12 curaṅkaḷtāṉ eṉṉuṭaya ātāram. eṉṉuṭaiya pustakaṅkaḷil nāṉ pēcukiṟa kaṭciyellām yāteṉṟāl cātāraṇa jaṉaṅkaḷukkuc caṅkītam kaṟṟuk koṭuppataṟku 12 curaṅkaḷālāṉa muṟaiyē veku culapam. ākaiyāl avaikaḷaiyē upayōkattiṟkuk koṇṭu vara vēṇṭum eṉpatē. āṉāl capaiyil vantirunta kalvimāṉkaḷum, caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum atinuṭpa curaṅkaḷai ēkōpittu oppukkoṇṭapōtu avarkaḷ tīrmāṉattiṟku yātoru taṭaiyumiṉṟi talai kuṉintu vaṇaṅkiṉēṉ. intapperiya kāṉpa reṉs ēṟpaṭṭu nāṉ colliya muṟaiyil niyāyattiṟku virōtamāṉatu oṉṟumillai yeṉṟu ceyta tīrppāṉatu eṉakku mikavum tiruptitāṉ. itu iyaṟkaitāṉē. āṉāl kaṭavuḷtāṉ aṅku piracaṉṉamāki naṭantavaikaḷuk kellām ātikāraṇarāyiruntār eṉṟu nāṉ niccayamākavē aṟintu vicuvācikkiṟapaṭiyāl eṉ kāriyam cittiyāṉataṟkāka nāṉ oru nāḷum perumai koḷḷamāṭṭēṉ.	*	*	*

(Sd.) V.N.BHATKANDE..
mēṟkaṇṭa kaṭitattāl ‘paṉṉiraṇṭu cuṅkaḷai ellōrum upayōkat tiṟkuk koṇṭu vara vēṇṭumeṉpatu eṉṉuṭaiya nōkkam. āṉāl capaiyil vantirunta kalvimāṉkaḷum, caṅkīta vitvāṉkaḷum ati nuṭpa curaṅkaḷai ēkōpittu oppukkoṇṭapōtu avarkaḷ tīrmāṉattiṟku nāṉ yātoru taṭaiyumiṉṟit talai kuṉintu vaṇaṅkiṉēṉ’ eṉṟu collu kiṟatait tāṅkaḷ kavaṉik vēṇṭum. curutikaḷaip paṟṟiyum, nuṭpa curutikaḷaip paṟṟiyum vīṇaiyilum vāyppāṭṭiṉālum, āyappālaiyil vaḻaṅkum 12 curaṅkaḷaiyum, vaṭṭappālaiyil vaḻaṅkum 24 curutikaḷaiyum, tirikōṇappālaiyil vaḻaṅkum 48 curutikaḷaiyum, caturappālaiyil vaḻaṅkum 96 curutikaḷaiyum nāṉ tiṣṭāntappaṭuttik kāṭṭiyapōtu tāṅkaḷum Mr.Bhatkande avarkaḷum pakkam pakkamāy vīṇaikkuc camīpattil iruntu kavaṉittuk koṇṭiruntīrkaḷ. tūrattilirunta uṅkaḷai  Mrs Atya Begum Fyzee Rahimin ammāḷ avarkaḷ kiṭṭavantu uṭkārumpaṭi varuntik kēṭṭuk koṇṭārkaḷ. avarkaḷālum maṟṟum capaiyiluḷḷa kaṉavāṉkaḷ yāvarālum oruṅkē atikamāy āccariyattōṭu koṇṭāṭappaṭṭa caṅkītam taṅkaḷukku māttiram aruvaruppāyiruntatu eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ.
nuṭpa curutikaḷai ovvoṉṟāy nālu pālaikaḷiṉpaṭi vevvēṟu kīrttaṉaṅkaḷil pōtumāṉa paṭi rucuppaṭuttikkāṭṭi itil āṣēpaṉai yirukkumāṉāl collavēṇṭum eṉṟu capaiyōraik kēṭkaiyil avarkaḷ evvita āṣēpaṉaiyum collāmal iruntārkaḷ. ippaṭic cāraṅkar curuti muṟai taṟkāla caṅkītattiṟku utavāteṉṟu rucuppaṭuttik kāṭṭum poḻutum karnāṭaka caṅkītattil vaḻaṅkivarum curutikaḷ Geometrical Progression paṭi varavēṇṭumeṉṟu collumpoḻutum nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷaip pāṭikkāṭṭi tiṣṭāntappaṭuttumpoḻutum āṣēpaṉai yiruntāl collavēṇṭumeṉṟu kēṭṭukkoṇṭēṉē.
akampāvattiṉāl capaiyōrai alaṭciyamāka nāṉ appaṭik kēṭka villai. periyōrkaḷ anēkar vantiruppārkaḷeṉṟum eṉ muṟaiyil tavaṟutalkaḷait tirutti aṉukkirakam ceyvārkaḷ eṉṟum niṉaittu mikavum vaṇakkamāyk kēṭṭuk koṇṭēṉ. āṣēpaṉai ceytiruntāl nuṭpa curutikaḷaip paṟṟi iṉṉum virivākac colli vistarittiruppēṉ. āṉāl tāṅkaḷ oppuk koṇṭataṟku iṇaṅka avarkaḷ aṉpum ātaravu māṉa pala iṉiya vacaṉaṅkaḷ colli āravāramum ceytārkaḷ. capaiyōr yāvarum oppukkoṇṭārkaḷ eṉṟu Mr.Bhatkande collukiṟataṟku māṟāka ‘itu rucuvalla’ eṉṟu collukiṟīrkaḷ. tāṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyattai rucuppaṭuttiviṭa vēṇṭumeṉṟu koṇṭuvantatupōla nāṉ karnāṭaka curuti muṟaikaḷai rucuppaṭutti stāpittu viṭalāmeṉṟu niṉaittu varavillai. intiyāvil ellā iṭaṅkaḷililumiruntu caṅkītattil tērnta kaṉavāṉkaḷ varum iṭattil pūrva tamiḻ nūliṉ apippirāyattaiyum taṟkālattiṉ aṉupōkattaiyum terivittu vaikka vēṇṭumeṉṟu nāṉ eṇṇiṉēṉ. tivāṉ cākip V.P.mātavarāv avarkaḷ viruppattiṟkum parōṭā makārājar avarkaḷaḻaippup pattirattiṟkum nāṉ kīḻppaṭiya vēṇṭumeṉṟu niṉaittēṉ. rucuppaṭuttiviṭuvataṟku aṉukūlamāka oruvaraiyum āmōtikkumpaṭi kēṭṭuk koḷḷavumillai. eṉ apippirāyattai tāṅki rippōrṭṭil eḻutuvārkaḷeṉṟu nāṉ niṉaikkavumillai.
31/2 maṇi nēramākavum ataṉpiṉ tāṅkaḷ coṉṉataṟkup patil collum viṣayamāka 3/4 maṇi nēramākavum ellōr maṉataiyum kavarntu koḷḷum paṭiyāka eṉ piracaṅkamum pāṭṭum iruntālum avaikaḷaik kāṉpareṉs muṭiyum camayattil eṭuttuc colla maṟantu pōṉārkaḷ. capaiyār yāvarālum taḷḷappaṭṭa ārmōṉiyattaik koṇṭu vanta taṅkaḷaip paṟṟiyum, taṅkaḷ cinēkitaraip paṟṟiyum, iṉṉuñ cilaraip paṟṟiyum māttiram rippōrṭ vācittu muṭittārkaḷ. ēṉ ippaṭic ceytīrkaḷ eṉṟu nāṉ kēṭkumpoḻutu avacaramāy rippōrṭ tayār ceytōm, maṟantu pōṉōm; iṉi cērttuk koḷvōm eṉṟu coṉṉārkaḷ. ivaiyāvum Fine arts, Mrs.Samuel aṟivār. capaiyi luḷḷa yāvaraiyum āccariyappaṭuttiyatu eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collum ik kāriyam viṭappaṭṭup pōṉataippaṟṟi nāṉ varuttappaṭavumillai. iṉi rippōrṭ eppaṭit tayār ceyvārkaḷ eṉṟu niṉaikkavumillai. eppaṭi yiruntālum “cattiyam pūmiyiliruntu muḷaikkum nīti vāṉattiliruntu tāḻappārkkum” (caṅ. 85.11) eṉṟa vēta vacaṉampōla ivaikaḷai iṉṉum cila kālattil pūraṇamāyk kāṇpīrkaḷ. nīṅkaḷ māttiram itai oru vēḷai kāṇāmal pōṉālum ulakattavar yāvarum kaṇṭu koḷvārkaḷ eṉpataṟku parōṭā kāṉpareṉsukku vantirunta capaiyār yāvarum oppukkoṇṭatē pōtumāṉa cākṣiyeṉṟu niṉaikkiṟēṉ. neruppukkup pukaiyum nīrukku nuraiyum pōla parōṭāvil kūṭiya āl intiya miyucik kāṉpareṉsukku tāṅkaḷum taṅkaḷaic cērnta cilarumiruppatu periya kāriyamalla.
LAKSHMIPURAM,
Mysore, 10-8-1916.
DEAR SIR,
In your Tamil letter of invitation, I was glad to find that you were going again to settle the question of Srutis. I heartly support your contention that Sharanga Dev was inaccurate in many respects, and that your exposition was most convincing. I appreciate only 3 or 4 papers that were presented in that Baroda Conference and yours was the most interesting to me of all. Those of Messrs. Clements and Deval were also learned, but the theories did not agree with their practical demonstrations. *    *     *     *     *
I agree to your division of the octave into 24 stutis and their demonstration through the help of your accomplished daughters. I am sure that the different notes used for the Ragas as expounded by you are correct.  *    *    *    *     *
If anything was striking to me in the Baroda Conference, it was your paper.
Wishing success to your earnest attempts. 
* 	* 	* 	* 	*
Yours truly,
(Sd.) H.P.KRISHNA RAO.
lakṣimipuram maicūr, 10-8-1916.
piriyamuḷḷa aiyā,
tāṅkaḷ eṉṉaik kāṉpareṉsukku aḻaitta (tamiḻil eḻutap paṭṭirunta) kaṭitattil kaṇṭa pirakāram curuti viṣayattaip paṟṟit tirumpa vicārikkap pōkiṟōm eṉṟu eḻutiyiruntatu eṉakku metta cantōṣam. cāraṅkatēvar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil picakippōyirukkiṟār eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ colvatai nāṉ maṉappūrvamāy oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayattai vistarittatāṉatu ellāruṭaiya maṉatilum naṉṟāyppaṭṭatu. parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil vācikkappaṭṭa upanniyācaṅkaḷil mūṉṟu allatu nālu viyācaṅkaḷ nāṉ atika vicēṣamāṉavaikaḷāka eṉ maṉatil paṭṭatu. avaikaḷil taṅkaḷuṭaiyatutāṉ ellāvaṟṟilum mēlāka eṉakkut tiruptikarattai uṇṭākkukiṟatu. Mr.kiḷameṇṭs tēvāl mutaliyavar kaḷuṭaiya upanniyācaṅkaḷ atika kalvit tiṟamaiyaik kāṭṭiṉa pōtilum avarkaḷuṭaiya muṟaikaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukkavillai.
oru stāyiyai tāṅkaḷ 24 cama pākaṅkaḷākap piritta muṟaiyaiyum taṅkaḷuṭaiya ciṟappu vāynta kalvit tiṟamaiyuḷḷa kumārattikaḷiṉ utaviyāl tāṅkaḷ atai rucuppaṭuttiyataiyum cariyeṉṟu oppuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ. pala irākaṅkaḷil varuvatākat tāṅkaḷ kāṇpitta curaṅkaḷ cariyeṉpataṟkuc cantēkamillai.
parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil eṉ maṉatil atikamāyp paṭṭatu taṅkaḷ upanniyācantāṉ.
taṅkaḷuṭaiya muyaṟcikaḷil kaṭavuḷ kūṭa iruntu avaikaḷaic cittipeṟac ceyya vēṇṭum eṉṟu pirārttikkiṟēṉ.
taṅkaḷ uṇmaiyuḷḷa,
(Sd.) H.P.KRISHNA RAO.
mēṟkaṇṭa kaṭitattil (1) cāraṅkatēvar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil tavaṟip pōyirukkiṟār eṉpatai maṉappūrvamāy oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ; (2) tāṅkaḷ caṅkīta viṣayattai vistarittatāṉatu ellōr maṉatilum naṉṟāyp paṭṭatu; (3) taṅkaḷuṭaiyatu (viyācam) tāṉ ellāvaṟṟilum mēlāka eṉakkut tiruptikarattai yuṇṭākkukiṟatu; (4) Mr.Clements, tēvāl mutaliyavar kaḷuṭaiya upanniyācaṅkaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukkavillai; (5) oru stāyiyai 24 camapākaṅkaḷākap pirippataiyum taṅkaḷ kumārattikaḷiṉ utaviyāl atai rucuppaṭuttiyataiyum cariyeṉṟu oppuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ; (6) pala irākaṅkaḷil varuvatākat tāṅkaḷ kāṇpitta curaṅkaḷ cariyeṉpataṟkuc cantēkamillai; (7) parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil eṉ maṉatil atikamākap paṭṭatu taṅkaḷ upanniyācantāṉ eṉṟu collum kuṟippukaḷait tāṅkaḷ kavaṉippīrkaḷāṉāl eṉ viyācattil colli yirukkum kuṟippukaḷ muṟṟilum cariyāṉavaiyeṉṟu taṅkaḷukku viḷaṅkum.
caṅkīta ratṉākararuṭaiya tuvāvimcati curuti muṟai taṟkāla caṅkītat tiṟku ottuvarātateṉṟu pala vitattilum rucuppaṭuttik kāṭṭiṉēṉ. taṅkaḷ kaṇita muṟaiyum taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyamum muṟṟilum ottuvaratavai yeṉṟu rucuppaṭuttiṉēṉ. oru stāyiyil paṉṉiraṇṭu 1/2 curaṅkaḷum irupattu nāṉku 1/4 curaṅkaḷum nāṟpatteṭṭu 1/8 curaṅkaḷum toṇṇūṟṟāṟu 1/16 curaṅkaḷum varukiṉṟaṉaveṉṟu kaṇita mūlamākavum vīṇaiyil kaṇṭa aḷavu mūlamākavum curam curutikaḷ varum irākaṅkaḷ mūlamākavum viḷakkiṉēṉ. im mūṉṟaiyum paṟṟi iṅkē collukiṟa vārttaikaḷait tāṅkaḷ kavaṉikka vēṇṭum.
‘cāraṅkar pala viṣayaṅkaḷil tavaṟippōyirukkiṟār. Mr.Clements, tēvāl muṟaikaḷ vāttiyaṅkaḷiṉ rucuvōṭu ottirukkavillai. curam curutikaḷait tāṅkaḷ rucuppaṭuttiyatai cariyeṉṟu oppukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ kāṇpitta curaṅkaḷ cariyeṉpataṟkuc cantēkamillai’ eṉṟu collum kuṟippukaḷ eṉ apippirāyam cariyeṉṟu colvataṟkup pōtumāṉavaiyallavā?  ivaikaḷaip pārkkilum nāṉ eṉṉa tiṣṭāntam koṭukkakkūṭum? ‘parōṭā kāṉpareṉsil eṉ maṉatil atikamāyppaṭṭatu taṅkaḷuṭaiya viyācantāṉ’ eṉṟu kalvit tiṟamaiyuḷḷavarum vaiṇīka vitvāṉumāyirukkiṟa oruvar collum cattiyattai nīṅkaḷ eppaṭi maṟukkakkūṭum? muḻu apattam eḻutiyikkiṟīrkaḷē. iṉṉum ippaṭippaṭṭa anēka kaṭitaṅkaḷ kāṭṭakkūṭum. ivarkaḷiruvarum parōṭā kāṉpa reṉsukku vantiruntavarkaḷ. ākaiyiṉāl ivarkaḷ iruvar kaṭitattai māttiram eṭuttukkoṇṭēṉ.
eṉṉuṭaiya curutimuṟai taḷḷappaṭṭatu. taṅkaḷ curuti muṟai yāvarālum aṅkīkarikkappaṭṭatu eṉṟu māttiram eḻutiyiruntāl nāṉ taṅkaḷaip perumai pārāṭṭic colla ētuvāyirukkum. ivviraṇṭu kuṟippukaḷukku māttiram patil eḻutiyiruppēṉ. āṉāl ivaikaḷōṭu kalanta maṟṟa kuṟippukaḷ avaṟṟiṟku patil eḻutum paṭiyāka eṉṉait tūṇṭiviṭṭaṉa. ellām eḻuti muṭinta piṉ avaikaḷuḷ ivviraṇṭaiyum paṟṟic colvatu avaciyamāyiṟṟu. taṅkaḷ ārmōṉiyam taḷḷap paṭṭa teṉṟu tāṅkaḷ oppukkoḷḷukiṟīrkaḷ. piḷḷaikaḷiṉ kāṉam cākrūṭiṉ cāyapu avarkaḷālum, maṟṟavarkaḷālum atikamāyp pukaḻappaṭṭatu (āccariya māy eṇṇappaṭṭatu) eṉṟum collukiṟīrkaḷ. ivviraṇṭu mukkiyamāṉa kuṟippukaḷaiyum tāṅkaḷē oppukkoṇṭatu yāvarālum kavaṉikkappaṭat takkatu.
ivviraṇṭu viṣayaṅkaḷil taṅkaḷ curuti muṟaiyum ārmōṉiyat tiluḷḷa curaṅkaḷum capaiyiluḷḷa yāvarālum aṉupōkattiṟku varātavai yeṉṟu taḷḷappaṭṭaṉa. tāṅkaḷum antac camayattil oppukkoṇṭu viṭṭataṉāl capaiyiluḷḷa oruvar pākkiyillāmal ellōrālum uṅkaḷ curutimuṟai taḷḷappaṭṭatākavillaiyā? appaṭiyē piḷḷaikaḷ pāṭiya karnāṭaka caṅkītamum oru stāyiyil 12, 24, 48, 96 pōṉṟa nāta vēṟṟumaikaḷum aṭaṅkiya nālu aṭṭavaṇaikaḷil pala irākaṅkaḷ vācittuk kāṭṭiyapōtu cākrūṭīṉ cāyapu avarkaḷum capaiyārummikunta āccariyap paṭṭārkaḷ eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collum poḻutu ituvaraiyum kāṇāmalum kēṭkāmalumirunta nūtaṉamāṉa oṉṟaik kaṇṭu kēṭṭu āṉantittārkaḷ eṉṟu tāṅkaḷ collukiṟatākat terikiṟatē. tāṅkaḷum piḷḷaikaḷiṉ camīpattiliruntu naṉṟāyk kavaṉittīrkaḷ. antac camayam tāṅkaḷ oṉṟum kuṟaicollavillai. ‘pukaḻntu koṇṭārkaḷ’ eṉpataṉāl capaiyiluḷḷōrum tāṅkaḷum eṉ curuti muṟaiyaiyum ataṉpaṭi pāṭiya pāṭṭaiyum oppuk koṇṭatāyiṟṟē. āṟumātattiṟku muṉ naṭantavaikaḷukku virōtamāy ippoḻutu colluvatu muṟṟilum cariyallaveṉṟu itaippārkkum aṟivāḷikaḷ yāvarum kāṇpārkaḷ.
uṇmaiyāṉa kaṇakkiṟkum iṉimaiyāṉa pāṭṭiṟkum aṉupōkamāṉa tiṣṭāntaṅkaḷukkum tāṅkaḷ koñcamāvatu acaiyāmal patileḻutak kūṭiya tīrar eṉṟu nāṉ niṉaikkiṟēṉ. intiya caṅkītattaip paṟṟi maṟṟa tēcattār tavaṟutalāy eṇṇumpaṭi tāṅkaḷ oru iṭaṟu kallā yiruppīrkaḷō eṉṟu tōṉṟiyatāl itai eḻutiṉēṉ.
taṅkaḷaip pōlavē teṉṉāṭṭil tuvāvimcati curuti eṉṟu vātāṭukiṟavarkaḷukku.
taṅkaḷaippōl oḻuṅkīṉamāṉa cura varicaikaḷaiyum, kutarkkaṅ kaḷaiyum collum palar innāṭṭilumiruntu teṉ intiya caṅkītattiṟkuk kuḻappam uṇṭākkukiṟatai aṟintu taṅkaḷukkum, maṟṟavarukkum ilakuvāy viḷaṅkak kūṭiyavaikaḷ evaikaḷō avaikaḷaiyē eḻutiṉēṉ.
1. ‘vīṇaiyil pañcamam kuṟaikiṟa’teṉṟu kāṉpareṉsil vātāṭic capaiyōrāl vīṇaiyil pañcamam caritāṉ eṉṟu tīrkkappaṭṭut tōlvi yaṭainta ceṉṉai mailāppūr cuntaramaiyarum,
2. irupattiraṇṭu curutiyiṉpaṭi oru tukkaṭā pāṭikkāṭṭa vēṇṭu meṉṟu kāṉpareṉsil kēṭṭapoḻutu capaimuṉ pāṭa muṭiyāmal oḷintu koṇṭa pūvaṉūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi piratāpa irāmacāmi pākavatar avarkaḷum,
3. ‘taṉṉiyāciyil kāntāram kuṟaintu varavēṇṭu’meṉṟu colli capaiyōrāl kūṭiyē vara vēṇṭum eṉṟu collakkēṭṭu mauṉampūṇṭa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi pañcāpakēca pākavatar avarkaḷum,
4. ‘oru stāyiyil ca-pa muṟaiyil 53 curutikaḷ varavēṇṭu’meṉṟu cātitta makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cuppiramaṇiya cāstiri avarkaḷum,
5. ‘cilappatikārattil caṅkītattaippaṟṟi iraṇṭu varitāṉ irukkiṉṟaṉa’ eṉṟu tañcai kāṉa capaiyil coṉṉa makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi T.N.irātākiruṣṇa aiyar B.A., avarkaḷum,
6. ‘oru stāyiyil 22 curutikaḷ varukiṉṟaṉa’ veṉṟu coṉṉa rāv pakatūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi nākōjirāv B.A. avarkaḷiṉ apippirāyattait tāṅki niṟkum makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi cuntaramaiyar B.A.,L.T. avarkaḷum,
7. ‘curuti viṣayam namatu puttikkeṭṭātatu’ ippoḻutu pirayōjaṉap paṭātatu, oru nāḷum muṭivu peṟāta cāstira caṇṭaiyuṭaiyatu, nuṭpamāṉa curutikaḷaik kavaṉittuk kīrttaṉaṅkaḷ pāṭuvataṟku anēka catur yukaṅkaḷāki viṭum, ivvitamāṉa cīrtiruttam ippōtu namakku vēṇṭām, tañcāvūr caṅkīta kāṉpareṉs 24 curutikaḷukkum 22 curutikaḷukkum ēṟpaṭṭa pōrk kaḷamāy muṭintatu eṉṟu eḻutiya makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi C.R. cīṉivāca aiyaṅkār B.A.avarkaḷum,
8. mailāppūr makā-rāca-rāca-ciṟi A.P.kaṇēca aiyar avarkaḷum iṉṉum ivarkaḷ pōtaṉaikkuṭpaṭṭa cila puṇṇiyavāṉkaḷum naṭantavaikaḷukku muṟṟilum virōtamākat taṅkaḷaippōl pēpparkaḷukku eḻutiṉārkaḷ.
ivarkaḷuṭaiya kaṭitam cilavaṟṟiṟku eṉatu cinēkitarkaḷ patil eḻuti yiruntārkaḷ. ellāvaṟṟiṟkum avarkaḷ eḻutavillai. nāṉum eḻuta niṉaikkavillai. āṉāl taṅkaḷ kaṭitattiṟku eḻutavēṇṭiyatu avaciya māyiṟṟu. atōṭu taṅkaḷaippōl pēpparukku eḻutiya teṉtēcattuk kaṉavāṉkaḷum aṟintukoḷvataṟku mukkiyamāy eḻutavēṇṭiyatāyiṟṟu.
maṟṟum mukkiyamāṉa cila kaṭitaṅkaḷaiyum - avaikaḷukku eḻutiya patilaiyum karuṇāmirta cākarattil ‘teṉṉintiya caṅkītattiṉ curutikaḷum āl intiya caṅkīta kāṉpareṉsum’ eṉṟa talaippiṉ kīḻk kāṇalām.
muṭivāka
(1) taṅkaḷ apippirāyattiṉpaṭiyum pūrvattōriṉ apippirāyaṅkaḷiṉ paṭiyum teṉṉintiyāviluḷḷa tavacirēṣṭarkaḷ apippirāyattiṉpaṭiyum tāṅkaḷ tiṣṭāntam koṭutta ēṇippaḻuvaip pōlavum camamāṉa ōcai yuṭaiya curaṅkaḷālāṉa caṅkītamē cariyāṉa caṅkītam.
(2) camamāṉa ōcaiyuṭaiya curaṅkaḷālāṉa caṅkītamē parōṭāvil eṉṉāl kāṭṭappaṭṭatu. ammuṟaiyē pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷiṉ cāstira ātārattiṟkum taṟkālaaṉupōkattiṟkum, aṇuppiramāṇamum picakāmal ottuvarakkūṭiyatu. iṉivarum kālattilum, yāvarālum oppuk koḷḷap paṭṭuk koṇṭāṭakkūṭiya muṟaiyeṉṟum caṅkīta cāstirattiṟkē putiya uyir nilai eṉṟum nāṉ niccayam colvēṉ. āṉāl taṅkaḷ oḻuṅkīṉa māṉa muṟai taḷḷappaṭṭup pōyiṟṟu.
(3) teṉṉintiyāvil piṭivātamāy tuvāvimcati curutiyeṉṟu cātikkum cilaraiyum muṉ piṉ aṟiyāmal oru stāyiyil 25 curutikaḷ eṉṟu cātikkum taṅkaḷaiyum tavira taṟkāla aṉupōkattaiyum pūrva muṟaikaḷaiyum kavaṉikkum aṟivāḷikaḷum iṉivarum cantatiyārum aṉuṣṭikkakkūṭiya uttamamāṉa muṟai eṉ muṟaiyēyeṉṟu nāṉ niccayamāyc colluvēṉ.
(4) curuti camamāy varavēṇṭumeṉṟa pūrva tamiḻ muṟaippaṭiyē pala aṉupōkaṅkaḷaik koṇṭu tiṣṭāntap paṭuttik kāṭṭuvēṉ. avai kaḷukku nēr virōtamāyc ceyyum taṅkaḷuṭaiya muṟai muṟṟilum oḻuṅkīṉamāṉateṉṟum oḻuṅkāyirukkum karnāṭaka caṅkītattaiyum intustāṉ caṅkītattaiyum keṭuttuk koṇṭirukkum eṉṟum nāṉ niccayamākac colvēṉ. tāṅkaḷ iṉi ippaṭic ceyyātirukkumpaṭi mikavum vaṇakkamāyk kēṭṭukkoḷḷukiṟēṉ. atōṭu tāṅkaḷ ippōtu eḻutiyirukkum kaṭitattaippōl eḻutuvīrkaḷāṉāl iṅkilīṣ caṅkīta māvatu karnāṭaka caṅkītamāvatu intustāṉ caṅkītamāvatu muṟṟilum teriyātavarkaḷeṉṟu maṟṟavarkaḷ uṅkaḷai ēḷaṉam ceyyumpaṭi nēriṭum. ēṉeṉṟāl pūrva tamiḻ makkaḷ āyappālaiyil vaḻaṅki vanta 12 curaṅkaḷum intustāṉ kītattilum, iṅkilīṣ caṅkītattilum vaḻaṅki varum curaṅkaḷum oṉṟākavē irukkiṉṟaṉa.
(5) parōṭā makā rājā avarkaḷ naṭattiya capaiyaiyum capaiyil vantirunta vitvāṉkaḷaiyum avamatikkiṟatōṭu aṅku naṭanta uṇmai kaḷai veḷiyiṭāmal ataṟku nēr virōtamāṉavaikaḷait tāṅkaḷ veḷiyiṭṭirukkiṟīrkaḷ. intiya caṅkītattiṟku ētāvatu naṉmai ceyya vēṇṭumeṉṟu tāṅkaḷ koṇṭa āvalai nāṉ mikavum meccik koḷḷukiṟēṉ.
(6) tāṅkaḷ eṇṇukiṟapaṭi oru kālattilum intiya caṅkītattai eṭuttu niṟutta taṅkaḷāl muṭiyāteṉṟu niccayam colluvēṉ. curutikaḷ cama aḷavuṭaiyavaikaḷāy varavēṇṭumeṉṟu coṉṉa pūrva teṉ tamiḻ muṉivarkaḷai ‘cāstirōktamillāta oru muṟaiyaik kaṇṭupiṭittāṉ’ eṉṟu coṉṉataṟkup patil avarkaḷ taṅkaḷ muṟaiyaiyē parikācak kūttākkiviṭṭārkaḷeṉṟu nīṅkaḷ naṉṟāy niṉaikka vēṇṭum.
(7) itaṉmuṉ caṅkīta viṣayamāy yātum aṟiyāta nāṉ vicārikkat toṭaṅkiya kālam mutal appōtaikkappōtu aṟintu koḷḷa vēṇṭiya aḷaviṟkut takuntapaṭi aṟiyātavaikaḷai aṟiyumpaṭi ceytu ivvaḷavu tūram eṉakku aṉukkirakam ceyta periyōr taṅkaḷukkum aṉuk kirakikkumpaṭi kaṭavuḷaip pirārttikkiṟēṉ.
aṉpuḷḷa turaiyē! taṅkaḷ kaṭitattiṟku vēlait tollaiyiṉāl patil eḻutak kūṭāmaliruntālum curukkamākat taṅkaḷukku itai eḻutiṉēṉ. eṉ vēlaikaḷaic ceyya vēṇṭiyiruppatāl taṟcamayam taṅkaḷiṭattil uttiravu peṟṟuk koḷḷukiṟēṉ. tāṅkaḷ eṉ muṟaippaṭi intiya caṅkītattiṉ uṇmaiyai aṟintukoḷvīrkaḷāṉāl cantōṣa maṭaivīrkaḷ. taṅkaḷukku eṉ aṉpāṉa vantaṉam.
taṅkaḷ uṇmaiyuḷḷa,
K.āpirakām paṇṭitar,
tañcāvūr.
LETTER NO.19
SHANTARAM HOUSE, MALABAR HILL,
BOMBAY.
Monday, 7th Aug. 16.
DEAR RAO SAHEB PANDITHER,
Many many thanks for the copies of your refutation of Mr.Clement’s letters to the Madras Mail as also for the two kind letters accompanying the same. I think I have already told you that I would never cease to admire your great labours and scholarship. If I live long enough I won’t be surprised to find you, one of these days, mentioned as the great leader of the Southern Music School.
I write to-day explaining generally my activities on this side and thereby removing any possible misapprehension that may have crept into your mind about my attitude towards some of the leading questions on the subject of music. I do not know which of my publications have come to your notice, but I hope you have seen my Hindustani Sangit Paddhati in Marathi. The Second Volume of the Paddhati briefly deals with the Shruti theories of our writers here. I have personally no Shruti theory of my own. The Shruti discussion in the beginning of the 2nd Volume of the Paddhati is practically a refutation of Mr. Deval’s theories by the Reductio ad absurdum method. The irony running through the chapter is patent to an intelligent Marathi reader. My publications Parijat Praveshika and Ragabodha Praveshika became necessary when Mr. Deval and his comrades were pressing Ahobala and Sommath into service. These publications put a stop to further mischief in that direction.
Then Sharangadeva was dragged in and became their sheet-anchor. I was not able to effectively dislodge them from that position with that success which you obtained the other day, I frankly admit.
But in the Paddhati I could show that Mr.Deval could not father his Shrutis on the author of Ratnakar. I shall now tell you, in brief, the whole history from our point of view.
I travelled for two or three months in the Southern Preisdency in search of useful information in the cold weather of 1904. I had learnet my Hindusthani music under first class masters and was thinking of taking some steps to evolve a tolerably workable music system for popular use on this side. I wanted a good rational and workable model for the same. I consulted the late Mr.Tirumalaya Naidu and Pandit Singarachary at Madras. Under their advice I visited Tanjore. I made then the acquaitance of Messrs. C. Nagoji Rao, P. Subrahmanya Shastri, Srinivas Rao, Ramanna, Jagannath Goswami, Panchapkesa Bhagavat, Muttaya Bhagvat, Seturam Das Swami and some others and freely discussed music with them through interpreters. P.Subrahmanya Sastri was not so well up in the subject then as he appears to be now. There was one thing which invariably came into my observation and it was this. The 12 Hindustani notes I sang to them were declared by the musicians there as their own 12 principal notes also. It was very encouraging to me. I was anxious ot obtain a system of Parent modes or Melakartas, which would be at once scientific and exhaustive for the classification of the 150 Ragams in use in our part of the country. My idea was that such a good foundation for the system would combine permanensce and rationality. I visited the Sarasvati Bhandara or Palace Library but did not find any Sanskrit Grantha there, which was likely to solve my dificulty. Jagannath Goswami did show me a Sanskrit Manuscript containing the 72 Melas and their Jayna Ragas, but the same was incomplete. I have already published that small work and called it Raga Lakshna, because the Swami said that was its name. From Tanjore I was directed by C. Nagoji Rao to Ettayapuram, where the late Subrama Dikshit Pandit lived. I learned good many things from that gentleman. He was really a great man and I liked him very much. He gave me a copy of the most valuable manuscript Chaturdandi Prakashika. He died before sending me the sfirst and the last chapters but I got almost all I wanted through my valuable friend, Mr. A. Krishnaswami Aiyar of Tinnelvelly. I have the highest respect for Venkatmakhi Pandit, who could write a work like that. I liked his frankness and powerful language as also his spirit. I visited Mysore, Ramnad, Rameshwar, Shrirang Madura and other places, but did not obtain much that, in my opinion, would be of material use to the Northern system of music. I knew full well that the northern system had many points quite peculiar to itself, but the fact that the principal 12 notes in the country were the same decided me to adopt chaturdandi’s 72 Melakarta system as a good basis for the Northern Ragas. The method of classifying Ragams under their Janaka Melas was a very old one and I saw no objection to adopt it for my design. The next three or four cold weather tours were undertaken by me to the Northern cities to satisfy myself that the Northern Musicians had none of their own independent systems, and to collect opinions on the question of differentiating characteristics of the different Ragas and so forth. I found Ratnakar and Darpana constantly cited as authorities in the north, but none who could rationally explain how they became useful. I visited Nagpur, Calcutta, Puri, Vijayanagar, Hyderabad, Nasik, Delhi, Agra, Jeypore, Mathura, Lucknow, Benares, Gaya, Baroda, Kathiawar, Karachi, Cutch, Lahore and several other places - but failed to meet a single decent Pandit who could argue the subject on the strength of any Sanskrit Granthas. I got much valuale practical information no doubt and I utilized all that in the books I have written.
(In my travels throughout India) Not a single Pandit could argue the Shruti question with anything like precision. No authorities were ever cited or discussed. Many made attempts to say that some of the Ragas admitted smaller tones than semitones but when pressed to explain and demonstrate with reasons and authorities they backed out. No grantha could be cited as authority for the distribution of the Shrutis, which therefore appeared to be to depend on personal whims. As to the use of the well-known 12 notes there was absolutely no disagreement.
I finished my last tour in 1909 and took up the work of writing my book. I retired from business for that purpose and devoted my whole time to the work. I first wrote the Sanskrit Lakshya Sangit, in which I included all that I had to say about the Hindusthani system. My friends who were in my confidence told me tha the theories in the book could not be followed quite clearly and asked me to write a commentary in Marathi. Thus the Hindustani Paddhati came into existence, I took, as I said, Chaturdandi Melakartas as my foundation and classified all the Northern Ragas thereunder. My friends tell me that my works are favourably received and that even the professionals accepted them as authoritative. I have cited Sanskrit Texts all through to show how the Ragas went through different phases before they assumed their present shapes which I have fully explained in all possible details and with due illustration. I won’t refer to that now and shall come to he point where Mr. Deval comes in.
Messrs. Deval and friends came in the mean while on the scene. They brought out the 22 Shrituis of the ancient Rishis of 2000 years ago. They supported them by quotations or rather misquotations from Parijat and Ragabodha. They said I was wrong in establishing a popular music system on the basis of 12 notes. They flourished their Dichord and dazzled their audiences. Mr.Clements interested himself in the subject and that added considerably to the strength of the combination. Mr. Deval was neither a musician nor a scholar, but the same could not be said of Mr. Clements. I wrote the 2 Praveshikas and showed that the 22 Shrutis of Deval had no basis in those books which they cited. The Phil-harmonic Society was my own suggestion and I was present at its first meeting at Satara, but I could not later on associate with its work which I knew to be wrong and had to keep aloof from it. In the meantime Mr.Clements brought out into prominence the great 22 Shruti harmonium and sought the patronage of the Governor and the Director of Public Instruction for the same. Indeed it was feared at one time that the instrument would have a place in every one of the Musical institutions in this Presidency, under the control of Government. The War came in and postponed the project. My Praveshikas had one effect. Mr.Deva. gave up his original stand on the the Granthas of Ahobala and Somnatha and quietly fathered the 22 Shrutis on Sharangadeva! That led to my including a chapter on the Shrutis in the 2nd Vol. of the Paddhati. The reductio ad absurdum process there is, as I said, patent to any Marathi reader My writings no doubt succeeded in throwing suspicion on Mr. Deval’s Shrutis, but the influences of Mr. Clements still invested his book with some importance and I should say capacity for mischief. Mr.Deval continued to give demonstrations of his Shrutis in the Southern Marata country but after my publications, he did not meet with the success he expected. He never ventured to bring his demonstrations to Bombay. His agitation was however causing me any amount of anxiety because it was quite unfairly destroying the useful work I was doing. I knew he was wrong but I could not cope with the influence of his champion Mr.Clements. I have a very great respect for Mr.Clements. He is a great scholar and takes real interest in Indian Music. I tried to explain matters to him in the right spirit but he was so fascinated with Deval’s Shrutis - perhaps he sincerely believed that Deval interpreted Sharangadeva right - that he practically refused to listen to me. He ignored me and my labours and set about distributing the 22 Shrutis among the Hindusthani Ragas with the help of musicins not carrying any very high reputation in the north. He began by giving 3 Shruti Ri and 3 Shruti Dha and Ati Komal Gqa and Atikomal Ni to the common Raga Kaphi. He said that was the real Shudha Scale of the ancient Rishis and munis as also of Sharangdevqa, commenced to evolve scales for Kalian, Khawaja. and etc. from that scale. This, I saw, was rather serious. The northern musicians, as also the Southern ones. used Chatushrutis Ri and Dha and Sadharama Ga, Kaishik Ni in Kaphi Ragam, and I told him so, but he said Mr. Deval was right and I was wrong, and went on with his new classifications. I drew his attention to this practice of the Vainikas in the country but was told that they were all playing wrong. He went the length of writing to me that it was the Vina players and the Nagsur players who had spoiled the real Hindusthani music. Reconcilliations between us thus became impossible. I appealed to Deval and requested him to correct the slight errors he had drifted into and thus come and co-operate with me. I told him I was not against the use of micro-tones or Shrutis in such of the Ragas as realy required them, but all I wanted was they should not be fathered on the Sanskrit writers so as to render their works rediculous. I proposed that we should fix the Shrutis for the Ragas in a sort of Conference of the Pandits and experts. He refused the offer saying he had gone too far to recede, and said he would stand or fall with his protector Mr.Clements. Thus a great cloud was hanging over my head. The position was this. Either Deval was right or I was, all my labours, perfectly honest and disinterested, were to come to nothing simply because Deval had a strong and influential friend and I had not.
But I had full confidence in my God. “Commit theyself unto God and trust in Him and He will bring it to pass,” was my motto. Who appealed sincerely to God and did not succeed? God Almighty saw that I was unjustly being swamped away by influential mischief-makers and decided to help me. He inspired H.H. The Gaekwar and his most sympathetic prime minister, the large-hearted Dewan Saheb, to take up my cause. Your great assistance also I ascrisbe to His inspiration. I take no credit to me for all that happened at the Conference. Mr. Deval and Mr. Clements and their great following collapsed like a pack of cards. The Sanskrit Professors corroborated all my interpretations and falsified Deval’s. I never had a Shruti Theory of my own. I relied upon the 12 notes which were firmly established throughout the country. My contention all through my books was that for popular education in music a system based on the established 12 notes was very convenient and therefore ought to be retained. Of course when the minute Shrutis were unanimously accepted by our scholars and practical experts, I had not the least objection to bow to their decision. It was naturally a great satisfaction to me that the great Conference came and decided that my contentions were not unreasonable. I shall never be elated with success because I know and honestly believe that it was He that was enacting all that was happening there.
I have nothing more to tell you now about my relations with Deval and his friends. I still love them as my friends and brothers because I know they too are working in the cause of our Indian Music with the same enthusiam. Such tifts are quite naqtural and unavoidable. They invariably lead to good results. I never claimed to be infallible myself. I have always corrected mistakes which I committed as will appear from my Hindusthani Paddhati. One must humbly go on working without regard to name or fame and leave it to Him to do the rest.
